top_10.title: Reproduce MinLod readback differences with a source-built texture fixture
top_10.body:
Refs #804. All 29 local records previously blocked by the MinLod operand compiled and built a D3D12 pipeline on WARP and RTX after the bridge fix. Under the tested synthetic bindings 19 wrote color on both adapters. Seven matched byte for byte and twelve had finite floating-point differences. That comparison alone does not identify the cause.

Claim one sampling form or adapter in a comment. Build on #804's source-built mip fixture. Start with one texture containing distinguishable colors at each mip, a defined sampler and coordinates, and one MinLod instruction form. Use an independent expected output with a stated error tolerance if filtering requires one.

- Run the translated shader and a direct desktop HLSL control on WARP and a physical adapter with the same texture, sampler and coordinates. Record the first differing pixel and channel. Separate finite output differences, unchanged clear values, timeouts and capability skips.
- Start at an exact mip level. Then vary one dimension such as the clamp near a mip boundary, gradients, or filter. Include a wrong-clamp or swapped-mip negative control and record the expected mismatch.
- Record the commit, DXC version, flags, adapter and driver, Windows build and debug-layer status. Publish the smallest source-built reproducer with results, or the tested range if the difference stays unreproduced. Keep archive shaders and other binary inputs local.

top_10.title: Run an independent EXE from archive input to two checked texture frames
top_10.body:
## Goal

Run an EXE with a different entry and dependency chain through archive input, decompression, texture upload and two checked D3D12 frames. Reuse the existing Zig 0.13.0 reader and pinned blast 1.3 fixture, the CPU-upload texture check from #814, and the per-frame submission and cleanup pattern in #829. This is the next integration test after #730.

## Scope

Use the two distinct generated archive records already used by `tests/cpu/archive_check.py`. Derive two small RGBA8 textures deterministically from the completed record bytes. Start with a byte-to-color rule and a point-sampled quad so the independent CPU reference can predict every pixel. Keep the same device and queue for both records. The EXE should decide when to publish each complete record, upload it, draw and wait.

## Acceptance

- Run the same source-built image under native Windows, `pe_map` and AOT. On WARP and a capable physical adapter, compare the decoded records, upload hashes, per-frame color bytes, completed fence values, cleanup counts and exit status.
- With two valid records, both frames match their independent references and the second uses the second texture. A stale-texture control must detect a predicted second-frame mismatch.
- Truncate the second record using the existing decoder failure case. Only the first completed record may be uploaded or displayed. Check that the tentative output from blast is withheld, allocations and GPU resources are released once, and the original failure status reaches the process exit.

To claim a slice, comment with the interface you would touch and any PR it depends on. The archive-to-texture fixture and GPU upload/verification can be prepared in parallel. Independent Windows results are welcome once the combined check is available.

Starting checks

```powershell
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_archive_blast$' -V
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_shim_upload_texture_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

AI-assisted.

top_10.title: Flaky: test_ws_bash_keeps_a_profile_appended_prompt_command and test_ws_bash_restores_an_inherited_prompt_command fail on the ubuntu-26.04 runner image
top_10.body:
## What

Two PTY integration tests fail on every run of the `kirocrew-linux-4-core` runners with `Image: ubuntu-26.04` (version `20261103.629`):

- `test/test_terminal_handler_pty_integration.py::TestTerminalWsIntegration::test_ws_bash_keeps_a_profile_appended_prompt_command`
- `test/test_terminal_handler_pty_integration.py::TestTerminalWsIntegration::test_ws_bash_restores_an_inherited_prompt_command`

Failure lines:

```
AssertionError: the profile's own PROMPT_COMMAND element did not survive the readiness hook's self-withdrawal.
AssertionError: the gateway's exported PROMPT_COMMAND was not restored after the readiness hook withdrew
```

The PTY tail shows `__systemd_osc_context_precmdline` and `OSC 3008` sequences. That image's bash profile appends its own systemd `PROMPT_COMMAND` element, which the tests do not expect.

## Why

Backend Tests (3.12, 7) goes red on unrelated PRs, and Coverage Gate fails closed behind it, so PR Readiness blocks. A rerun lands on the same image and fails again.

## Additional Context

- OS: Linux, `ubuntu-26.04` runner image.
- Seen on #36815 (heads `720eb61`, rerun included, and `689acf5`): https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/43760844876/job/132958102857
- Same two tests on another PR: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/43722317344
- Main's shard 7 passed in the same window on a different runner pool: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/43725366454
- Both tests pass locally, and neither file changed on main.
- Likely fix: have the tests tolerate (or strip) an image-supplied `PROMPT_COMMAND` element, or run them with a profile that the image cannot extend.

issues.title: [doc-audit] 03-indexing.md BTreeDirectoryEntry shows Reserved field but source has Slot; StableId claimed as sole lookup key
issues.body:
**Doc path:line:** `doc/in-depth-overview/03-indexing.md` lines 295–304

**Wrong sentence(s):**
Line 298 of the struct listing:
```csharp
    public short Reserved;
```
Line 304:
> `StableId` is the lookup key: `-1` is the convention for the PK index, positive values are `FieldInfo.FieldId` for secondary indexes, `0` is for standalone/test trees.

**Contradicting code:**
`src/Typhon.Engine/Indexing/internals/BTree.cs` lines 73–88 and 91–135

The second field is *not* `Reserved` — it is `Slot` with a full doc comment:
```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Component slot within the archetype, for the per-archetype index segments that several
/// component slots share; 0 on a per-ComponentTable segment, which hosts one component's trees only.
/// See <see cref="BTreeStableKey"/> for why the slot is part of the key (#657).
/// </summary>
public short Slot;
```
And lines 91–98 of `BTree.cs` explicitly state:
> `StableId` alone is NOT unique on a per-archetype index segment. Field ids restart at 0 for every component, so two components in the same archetype that each index their field #0 both register with StableId 0. Creation appends two distinct entries and works, but on reopen `FindInDirectory` returns the FIRST match for both trees — they end up sharing one root…

The actual lookup key is the *pair* `(StableId, Slot)` via `BTreeStableKey` (lines 104–135).

**Suggested fix:**
1. Replace `public short Reserved;` with `public short Slot;      // component slot within archetype; 0 on per-CT segments`
2. Change "StableId is the lookup key" to: "The lookup key is the pair `(StableId, Slot)`: `StableId` is `-1` for the PK index, `FieldInfo.FieldId` for secondary indexes, or `0` for standalone/test trees; `Slot` is the component's slot within the archetype, which disambiguates two components in the same archetype that share a `StableId` value (issue #657)."

issues.title: [doc-audit] 02-storage.md states DatabaseFormatRevision is 4; source is 8
issues.body:
## Finding

`doc/in-depth-overview/02-storage.md` has two places that claim format version 4:

- **Line 154** section header: `### The first eight pages of an empty file (format v4)`
- **Line 178** struct sample comment: `public int DatabaseFormatRevision; // currently 4 (CK-05 twins + directory-only root)`

## Source

`src/Typhon.Engine/Storage/internals/PagedMMF.cs:123`:
```csharp
internal const int DatabaseFormatRevision = 8;
```
Version history in that file: v5 = WorldTick entity keys, v6 = per-sector page verification, v8 = entity-level spatial index removed (#872 step 13).

## Impact

Anyone checking format compatibility against the doc will read the wrong constant. The struct sample is what readers copy when writing tooling against the file format.

## Fix

Update the section header to `(format v8)` and update the struct comment to `// currently 8` with a brief note about the version history (or simply remove the parenthetical comment).

issues.title: [doc-audit] tick-lifecycle WorkerCount default omits Math.Max(1, ...) floor
issues.body:
## Finding

`doc/feature-set/Runtime/tick-lifecycle/README.md` line 60:

```
| RuntimeOptions.WorkerCount | -1 (`ProcessorCount - 4`) | Worker threads ... |
```

## Source

`src/Typhon.Engine/Runtime/public/RuntimeOptions.cs`:
```csharp
internal int ResolveWorkerCount() => WorkerCount == -1 ? Math.Max(1, Environment.ProcessorCount - 4) : WorkerCount;
```

## Impact

On a 4-core (or fewer) machine the doc implies 0 workers, but the engine clamps to 1. Minor but factually wrong.

## Fix

Change the default description to `-1 (`Math.Max(1, ProcessorCount - 4)`)`.

issues.title: [doc-audit] 01-foundation.md claims AccessControlSmall has no promoter logic but TryPromoteToExclusiveAccess exists
issues.body:
**Doc path:line:** `doc/in-depth-overview/01-foundation.md` line 70

**Wrong sentence:**
> No re-entrancy. No promoter logic. Same `WaitContext` integration.

**Contradicting code:**
`src/Typhon.Engine/Foundation/Concurrency/internals/AccessControlSmall.cs` lines 366–430

The struct provides a full Shared→Exclusive promotion API:
```csharp
// line 370
public bool TryPromoteToExclusiveAccess(ref WaitContext ctx)

// line 419
public void DemoteFromExclusiveAccess()
```

The dedicated feature page (`doc/feature-set/Foundation/access-control-lock-family/access-control-small.md` line 48) already correctly notes: "continuous shared acquisitions can starve a pending exclusive/promote", so the overview and the feature page contradict each other.

The distinction worth preserving is that `AccessControlSmall` lacks *waiter preference counters* (the per-promoter-waiter tracking that the full `AccessControl` has in its high bits), so promotion can be starved — it's not that promotion is absent.

**Suggested fix:**
Replace "No promoter logic." with "Promotion is supported (`TryPromoteToExclusiveAccess`/`DemoteFromExclusiveAccess`) but has no waiter-preference counter — continuous shared acquisitions can starve a pending promote."

issues.title: Check required inputs before long agent runs
issues.body:
## Problem

Long agent runs can start without all required inputs. Text may arrive while images or other attachments do not.

The run can then complete against incomplete evidence.

Katie Parrott’s [early-access Fable 5.2 review](https://every.to/vibe-check/fable-5-2) reports an overnight agent run that analyzed slide text but missed deck screenshots. This is an observation, not an independently verified benchmark.

## Change

Add a preflight that inventories required inputs before a long EGM run begins.

The preflight must confirm that the agent can read each required input. It must distinguish text, images, and other attachments.

Stop the run with an actionable error when a required input is absent or unreadable.

## Acceptance criteria

- The run defines its required inputs before execution.
- The preflight confirms the count, type, and identity of each input.
- The preflight verifies that the agent can read each input.
- The run stops before execution when a required input is absent or unreadable.
- The run records the preflight result.
- Automated tests cover text-only input, mixed text and images, a missing image, and an unreadable attachment.

`test/test_subagent_scale_batch.py::TestCoalescer::test_tool_merge_clears_stale_retrying_attempt` failed on an unrelated PR.

- Run: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/41797479802/job/126467561880 (PR #29490, head 712e6f822c65)
- OS: ubuntu, Python 3.12, Backend Tests shard 3
- Failing line: `((etype, data),) = all_frames` -> `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)`

The test waits a fixed `await asyncio.sleep(0.06)` past the 20 ms flush tick and then expects one frame. On a slow runner the flush has not happened yet, so the list is empty. It passes 8/8 locally (alone and with the whole file under -n 4). PR #29490 does not touch the coalescer or this test.

Likely fix: wait for the frame (poll with a deadline) instead of a fixed sleep.

issues.title: Church name text hidden in sidebar but still shown on login page when a custom logo is uploaded
issues.body:
## Description When a custom church logo is uploaded (Admin → System → Church Information), the church-name text is hidden in the sidebar but still shown on the login page — inconsistent behavior across the two surfaces that both render the logo. - **Sidebar** (`src/Include/Header.php`, lines ~186-199): the `navbar-brand-text` span is wrapped in `if (ChurchLogoService::hasCustomLogo())` — it only renders when there's **no** custom logo: ```php 'navbar-brand-image crm-brand-logo']) ?> ... ``` - **Login page** (`src/session/templates/begin-session.php`, lines 30-37): `ChurchLogo::img()` and `ChurchMetaData::getChurchName()` render unconditionally as separate elements, with no `hasCustomLogo()` check at all: ```php

``` Confirmed identical on both `master` and the `7.8.1` tag (same blob SHA on `begin-session.php` across both refs). The sidebar's hide-on-custom-logo behavior was intentional per #9719 ("The uploaded logo replaces the ChurchCRM branding in the sidebar (where it also hides the church-name text)") on the assumption that an uploaded logo already contains the church name as artwork. The login page not following the same rule means that assumption isn't applied consistently — admins who want the name visible lose it in the sidebar but keep it on login, with no way to choose. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Admin → System → Church Information → upload a custom logo. 2. Visit the dashboard — sidebar shows only the logo, no church name. 3. Log out and view the login page — logo **and** church name are both shown. ## Expected Consistent behavior between the sidebar and the login page — either both hide the name when a custom logo is present, or neither does. ## Reported by maestrovivo, in the project's Discord #support-chat.

From a full audit of the tree at 47a962a (3.5.0 + #452) on 2026-11-12. Each finding was checked against the code, reproduced where it can be run, and then checked again by a second reviewer who tried to refute it. Findings that were refuted, already decided in `docs/design-decisions.md`, or already filed are left out. The severity is the second reviewer's. The reproduction and suggested fix for each one are in the audit record (ask on this issue to have one posted).

**26 findings: 0 high, 7 medium, 19 low.** Tick a box and name the PR when a fix is merged.

Contract, SKILL.md and references:

- [ ] **medium** `SKILL.md:109` (A191): Two SKILL.md routing rows give commands that fail on every input: `fit.py --duration 2x` and `background.py` without --width/--height
- [ ] **medium** `docs/contract.md:225` (A197): docs/contract.md's role, verification-policy and visual-check tables still describe a 21-tool subset; "requires_visual_verification is true exactly for" names 8 tools, while the JSON and its test have 27

issues.title: fix(ci): migrate reusable eval workflows to the Go CLI and require real automatic-run artifacts
issues.body:
## Summary

<!-- 2-4 sentences: describe the bug, feature request, documentation gap, or task. -->

The reusable `waza.yaml` workflow still installs a Python package and uses obsolete CLI/result contracts, while automatic `waza-eval.yml` runs do not resolve output defaults before execution. A successful current-main automatic evaluation run uploaded no result artifact. Migrate retained consumer workflows and examples to one tested Go CLI contract; proposed target v0.41.0.

## Type of issue

- [x] Bug
- [ ] Feature request
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Maintenance
- [ ] Question or investigation

## Agent instructions

<!-- Make this actionable for a coding agent. Include constraints, likely files, and what not to change. -->

- Goal: Every advertised reusable workflow invokes the actual Go Waza contract, preserves meaningful failures, and produces usable evidence on push/PR/dispatch/call events.
- In scope: Installation/source-version strategy, supported arguments, effective input defaults, result/output mapping, artifact verification, and corresponding CI guide/site examples.
- Out of scope: Reintroducing Python Waza, altering product exit/reporting policies to accommodate stale examples, silently changing callers' output names, or using mutable latest installs as exact-source regression evidence.
- Likely files or areas: `.github/workflows/waza.yaml`, `waza-eval.yml`, `skills-ci-example.yml`, `docs/CI-CD-GUIDE.md`, site CI documentation and workflow contract tests.
- Dependencies or related issues: Coordinate final enforcement with [#900](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/issues/900). Keep reporter product bug [#892](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/issues/892) separate; this issue fixes workflow consumption and result evidence, not the reporter implementation.

## Current behavior

<!-- What happens today? For bugs, include the actual result and error output if available. -->

[`waza.yaml`](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c/.github/workflows/waza.yaml#L48-L81) runs `pip install waza`, `--format json`, `--fail-threshold`, `waza report`, and reads `.summary.pass_rate` / `.summary.composite_score`. Current Go run accepts `default` or `github-comment` output format and writes native summary fields such as `success_rate`; there is no corresponding `cmd_report.go` command. In [`waza-eval.yml`](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c/.github/workflows/waza-eval.yml#L154-L197), `OUTPUT_FILE` reads a raw input that is empty on automatic events, but upload falls back to `results.json`. [Current-main run 41918346222](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/actions/runs/41918346222) succeeded, warned `No files were found with the provided path: results.json`, and its artifacts API returned an empty list. The CI guide repeats obsolete summary keys/actions, so documentation can propagate the mismatch.

## Expected behavior

<!-- What should happen instead? For feature requests, describe the desired outcome. -->

Resolve effective defaults once for all event types and use the same values for execution, parsing, summary, and upload. Use a reviewed Go installation/build strategy with genuine embedded dashboard assets where source builds require them. Validate result shape, completeness, and availability instead of interpreting null/missing values as zero or success. Preserve documented reusable inputs/outputs through migration or explicitly document reviewed breaking changes.

## Steps to reproduce

<!-- For bugs, provide the smallest reproducible example. Delete if not applicable. -->

1. Inspect the historical Python workflow against `cmd/waza/cmd_run.go` and `internal/models/outcome.go` at the cited SHA.
2. Read the current-main automatic run log's artifact warning.
3. Query `GET /repos/microsoft/waza/actions/runs/41918346222/artifacts` and compare the empty list with the workflow's stated result-artifact contract.

## Environment

<!-- Fill in what you know. Delete fields that are not relevant. -->

- OS: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu.
- Waza version or commit: `f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c`.
- Go version: CI specifies 1.26; stale reusable workflow provisions Python 3.11.
- Command run: Read-only `gh run view 41918346222 --log`, artifacts API, and local CLI/model source reads.

## Acceptance criteria

<!-- Use checkboxes so an agent can verify completion directly. -->

- [ ] Retained reusable workflows install/build the intended Go version and invoke supported commands and flags.
- [ ] Push, PR, workflow_dispatch, and workflow_call paths resolve identical defaults; explicit custom output/context inputs remain intact.
- [ ] Actual CLI fixtures cover passing grading, completed failing grading, task/runtime errors, missing/malformed artifacts, zero scores, and absent values without success-shaped fallbacks.
- [ ] Automatic successful runs must upload a fresh, complete result artifact; missing evidence fails rather than only warning.
- [ ] Workflow outputs and thresholds use validated current producer fields and preserve failure exit policy.
- [ ] Copied CI guide/site workflows are exercised by contract tests against actual CLI help and saved JSON; unsupported legacy actions/installation examples are migrated or explicitly retired.

## Validation expectations

<!-- List expected automated or manual checks, or say why validation is not applicable. -->

- [ ] Applicable `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `golangci-lint run`.
- [ ] `NO_COLOR=1 make test-compat` for behavior-affecting workflow/CLI contracts.
- [ ] Docs site checked, if docs changed: build and Chromium e2e; documentation example controls execute copied commands.
- [ ] Web/dashboard checks run, if `web/` changes.
- [ ] Other: event/default mutation controls and production-CLI fixture runs with a rejecting offline runtime; verify actual uploaded artifact content on current-head CI.

## Additional context

<!-- Add links, screenshots, logs, related issues, or implementation notes. -->

Research date: 2026-11-06. The Python workflow was identified statically; no third-party Python package was installed or executed. The missing automatic-run artifact is directly observed, not inferred.

issues.title: [Request] 文档：Secure Boot 开启下的自签流程（db 自签 / MOK+shim）与三个已知坑
issues.body:
> 起草说明：本文由 AI 辅助整理，事实来自仓库现状与 #145 的讨论；**没有做真机验证**（我这台没有可切 Secure Boot 的独显机位），凡未实测之处都已标注。若与现场不符，以现场为准。

### 建议类型 / Request type

文档修正 / Documentation change

### 当前问题与需求 / Current problem and need

**要解决的是文档缺口，不是功能缺口。** 想让 Secure Boot 保持开启的用户，现在在文档里只能读到一句：

- `docs/faq.md:272` / `docs/faq.en.md:263`：`替换 U 盘启动文件前先备份。Secure Boot 关闭或使用受信任的自签 EFI。`

这句话承认了自签这条路存在，但没有过程。而 [#145](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/145)（已关闭）里三条路只写全了一条：

| #145 里的方案 | 文档状态 |
|---|---|
| 方案一 休眠切换法（SB 开/关来回切） | 评论里有完整流程，未入 FAQ |
| 方案二 固件内置 FFS（PR #100） | `docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162` 有可行性，标注【待实证】 |
| 方案三 MOK + shim | 评论里有六步，未入 FAQ |
| 方案三 db 自签 | **只有"简版"一句**：每台机器手动导证书、每次更新重签 |

而现场反馈指向的恰恰是最后这条：#145 里有一条西语报告——"Conseguí firmar con un certificado propio el Efi, de modo que ha sido posible iniciar con el secure boot activado"（用自己的证书签了 EFI，因此可以在 Secure Boot 开启下启动）。这是 db 自签路线**可用**的现场证据，但它现在埋在一条已关闭的 issue 的评论区里，既没进 FAQ，也没进兼容性记录。

现实需求面也不小：#145 的原始动机是打 LoL/Vanguard（反作弊要求 SB 开启），而 `docs/community-reports.md` 里的实测行几乎每条都写着 "Secure Boot off"——SB-on 场景目前是文档空白区。

补充一点定位：这**不是**在申请"绕过 Secure Boot"。自签属 `SECURITY.md:53` 威胁模型里"已开启 Secure Boot 且已导入自签证书"的合法配置，与方案一、方案二并列，只是缺文档。

### 期望改进 / Desired improvement

新增 `docs/faq.md#secureboot`（EN 同步 `docs/faq.en.md`）一节，建议内容：

1. **两条路线对比表**：db 自签（固件直接验你的签名，代价是每台导证 + 每次重签）vs MOK+shim（不动 db，走发行版 shim）。shim 那条直接链接 #145 现有六步，不重复写。
2. **db 自签五步**：
   - 生成密钥/证书（`openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -addext "extendedKeyUsage=codeSigning"`——这个 EKU 不能省，Windows 侧 `signtool` 会校验）；
   - 签名与验证（`sbsign --key ... --cert ... --output ...`；`sbverify --cert ...`；Windows 等价物 `signtool sign /fd SHA256` + `signtool verify /pa`）；
   - 把 **DER 证书追加**进 db 的三种方式：固件 Key Management（`db → Append / Append from file`）、`efitools` 的 `efi-updatevar -a -c cert.crt -k KEK.key db`、`sbctl enroll-keys --microsoft`（`--microsoft` 才会把微软证书一并写回）；
   - 新版 maker 直接吃签名后的件：`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284`（`-BootEfi`）、`:488`（盘根）、`:494`（`EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI`），即
     ```powershell
     .\make-usbroot.ps1 -Family ad102 -Out G:\ -BootEfi .\BOOTX64.signed.efi
     ```
   - 验证：`mokutil --sb-state` 应为 `SecureBoot enabled`；固件层真正放行的铁证是盘上出现新的 `loader.log` 且含 `TX BUILD` banner。
3. **三条硬纪律**（这部分比签名本身更容易出事）：
   - **只能追加，不能替换 db 里的微软证书**——`bootmgfw.efi` 靠 *Microsoft Windows Production PCA 2011* 签名，删了 Windows 起不来；
   - **动 PK 前先导出 PK/KEK/db 备份**；若板子要求清 PK 进 Setup Mode 才能 Append，事后必须把原厂证书恢复并重新 enroll PK；
   - **私钥只留本机**：db 里一旦有你的证书，这把私钥就能给这台机器签任何引导组件。
4. **三个已知坑**：
   - **SB 开着时 `ssdiag` 仍然不可用**：它临时加载的 `pmxdrv.sys` 是 Intel/COMODO 2018 交叉签名、无微软根，SB-ON 必然被 DSE 拒（`tools/ssdiag/README.md` 的 "Secure Boot — the gate that actually refuses this driver"、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`）。所以 SB 常开的机器上，系统内读回只能走 `loader.log` 的 `HANDOFF-OUT`（EFI 阶段零驱动读回）或 Linux 侧 `tools/diag-unlock.py`；要 `ssdiag --reapply` 修回锁，仍须临时关一次 SB。
   - **BitLocker / PCR[7]**：SB 或 db 状态变化会改 PCR[7]，可能弹恢复密钥，操作前先挂起保护。
   - **换版本必须重签**，签名后再改一个字节即失效；资产 `*.bin` 不需要签名（SB 只验 PE 引导链）。
5. **反作弊边界**（与 #145 的警告保持一致）：db 自签不改 SB 状态位，Vanguard（LoL）通常可过；ACE 系（腾讯）会校验 TPM/PCR[7] 链式启动记录，自签链的度量与原厂引导不同，**不保证过检**——打 ACE 系游戏请回到方案一。

顺带把 `docs/faq.md:272` / `.en.md:263` 那句改成带锚点的链接。

### 相关版本、文档与参考资料 / Versions, documentation and references

- 文档现状：`docs/faq.md:272`、`docs/faq.en.md:263`（自签仅一句）
- 讨论：#145（休眠切换法、FFS 方案、MOK+shim 六步、db 自签简版）；西语现场反馈在该 issue 评论中
- 固件形态可行性：`docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162`（SB 只验 OS 引导链）
- maker 的 boot 路径改动：`5684752`（打印可执行 copy 步骤）、`c0f3518`（输出不再纯平铺）、`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284/488/494/500/505-511`
- ssdiag 的 SB 门：`tools/ssdiag/README.md`、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`
- 威胁模型定位：`SECURITY.md:53`
- FAQ 判据/回锁值（本 issue 不涉及，仅说明读回路径不同）：`docs/faq.md:189`、`docs/cold-values.md:139`

### 替代方案与补充信息 / Alternatives and additional context

- **替代**：维持现状，让每个 SB-on 用户自己在 Discussions 问一遍。现状的代价是 #145 已经被关掉，新来的人搜不到过程。
- **更小的一步**：只把这份内容作为 #145 的补充评论贴回去——但该单已关闭，不解决"下次还能找到吗"。
- **我愿意直接出 patch**：如果维护者认可，可以照 #141 / #144 的方式提 docs PR，中英同步、只动 `docs/faq*.md`。
- **缺一个现场字段**：能否请 #145 那位西语报告者补 **主板型号** 与 **`ssdiag` 是否被拒**（第 4 条里"必然被拒"还是"通常被拒"取决于此），以及 **BitLocker 是否弹过恢复密钥**。这三项决定文档该写成硬性结论还是保守表述。

issues.title: [Report] RTX 4060 Laptop (28A0) / MECHREVO Yaoshi15Pro 2024 (GM5IX0A, i7-14650HX) - v2.1.9 TX success, matched A/B FP16 +81%, 15-inch thin laptop @ 140 W
issues.body:
## 摘要 / Summary

`10de:28a0`（AD107 · 24 SM · 8 GB）在机械革命 **耀世15Pro 2024**（i7-14650HX / 32 GB）上完成 **v2.1.9 Ada 事务**，EFI 侧读回全绿（`HANDOFF-OUT: ss0=0x88888888 ss1=0x8 readout1=0x00000000 feat_plm=0xffffffff`），Windows 正常进入。

**平台定位需要先说明**：这是一台 **15 寸轻薄游戏本**，不是同 TGP 的厚砖机。140 W 塞进这个厚度的机身，散热余量本来就是这个形态的短板——下面的 87 ℃ / 2.5 GHz 持续数据要放在这个前提下看，不代表其他 140 W 机型的水平。

同一脚本、同一 GPU 设置（140 W / 核心 +105 MHz / 显存 +200 MHz）的前后对照：

| 路径 | 解锁前 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.26 / 21.27 | **38.45** | **+81%** |
| BF16 | 21.25 / 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 / 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3 | 40.79 / 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（对照） | 6.41 / 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |

## 性能对比 / Performance comparison

**口径**：`make-usbroot.ps1` 自带前的自写脚本 `gemm_bench.py`（`torch.mm`，8192 系尺寸扫，`cudaEvent` 计时，每尺寸 5 次预热 + 3 窗口 × 20 次取中位），**解锁前后同脚本、同 GPU 设置**；解锁前为上一次启动（stock），解锁后为事务后同一次启动，两次测量间隔约 40 分钟，期间未改任何 GPU 设置。

**A/B（N=4096，TF/s）**

| 路径 | stock 第1次 | stock 第2次 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.27 | 21.26 | **38.45** | +81% |
| BF16 | 21.25 | 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 | 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3（`_scaled_mm`） | 40.79 | 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（TF32 off，对照） | 6.41 | 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |
| 显存 copy（对照） | 153.8 GB/s | 153.0 GB/s | 150.0 GB/s | 持平 |

`FP16 / FP8` 比值：stock 0.52 → 解锁后 0.51；`FP16 / FP32` 比值：stock 3.1× → 解锁后 5.9×。三条对照（FP32、显存带宽、以及时钟本身）都持平，说明增益不是时钟或散热瞬态造成的。

**其他尺寸（解锁后，同一脚本）**：FP16 1024 → 42.51，4096 → 38.45，8192 → 35.46。

**第二套独立基准交叉验证**：用 [#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119) 附件里的 `baseline-gemm-v1.py` 原样跑（N=4096、`torch.mm(a,b,out=c)`、7 组 × 30 次、每组一个 event 窗口）：**FP16 37.587 TF/s，BF16 38.227 TF/s**，与本机自写脚本的 38.45 / 38.66 一致（差 2%）。

**持续负载（解锁后，FP16 GEMM 4096，连续 40 s）**

| 指标 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 吞吐 | 36.06 TF/s（40 s 平均） |
| 核心时钟 | 2625 → 2430 MHz，均值 **2545 MHz** |
| 功耗 | 均值 132 W，峰值 **139.8 W**（顶死 140 W TGP） |
| 温度 | 79 → **87 ℃**（控制台 `TargetTemperature` 即为 87） |

**与现有报告的对比（仅供维护者参考，不作结论）**：[#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119)（28e0）stock 29.51 → 44.24；[#124](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/124)（2882 桌面）n=4096 FP16 26.98 → 42.44。本机 stock 21.26 明显更低但增益更大（+81% vs +49% / +57%）。解锁后绝对值低 13–15%，而 **每 MHz 效率与 #119 接近**（本机 36.06 / 2545 MHz ≈ 14.2 GFLOPS/MHz；按其 44.24 反推约 3.0 GHz 得 ~14.7），因此**我倾向于认为这是 140 W 笔记本散热包络下的频率差异，而非解锁不完整**——这一条是假设，没有 ssdiag 读回佐证。

issues.title: First time contributing? Start here.
issues.body:
Welcome 👋

If you've never contributed to AiSOC before, here's the shortest path from "interesting repo" to "merged PR".

## Step 1 — See AiSOC actually running

```bash
git clone https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC && cd AiSOC
make up      # the CORE profile — the real pipeline
make smoke   # prove it: one real event in, a retrievable alert out
```

`make up` creates `.env`, generates every secret in it, creates an administrator and **prints its password once** — copy it. Then sign in at <http://localhost:3000> (API docs at <http://localhost:8000/api/docs>). `make smoke` reports PASS or FAIL for each stage, so you know the pipeline works rather than assuming it:

```
[PASS] raw telemetry accepted by ingest
[PASS] event traversed the spine and became an alert
[PASS] alert is retrievable by id from the API
```

Needs Docker Compose v2 with 8 GB memory and 20 GB free disk in the Docker VM, plus `python3` and `bash`. `make doctor` checks all of it and diagnoses a stack that won't come up. [Installation](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/installation) says what each number was measured against.

**Zero install:** [open in GitHub Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/beenuar/AiSOC?quickstart=1) and run the same commands, then click the forwarded port 3000 in the **Ports** panel.

Once it's up, `make demo` loads labelled synthetic data on top — including `/cases/INC-RT-001?tab=ledger`, a LockBit 3.0 ransomware case the agent has investigated. Click through the **Investigation Ledger** so you've seen what AiSOC does. Every seeded row carries `is_synthetic=true` and the console labels it as such.

> One thing to avoid: `pnpm aisoc:demo` brings up `infra/compose/docker-compose.demo.yml`, which is a **UI preview only** — no ingest service, no fusion service, and Kafka disabled. The file says so in its own header. It's fine for looking at the interface, but it can't tell you whether AiSOC works. Use `make up` for that.

## Step 2 — Pick a small, scoped task

The [`good first issue`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) list is the first place to look — comment on one saying you'd like to take it. It's often thin, so these standing tasks are always open:

- **Add a detection.** New rules go under [`detections/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections) with positive *and* negative fixtures in [`detections/fixtures/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections/fixtures). Read [`detections/README.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/detections/README.md) first — it explains the four tiers and what "executable" means here (a rule replayed through the real engine and watched to fire, which is not the same as a rule that detects an attack).
- **Add a connector.** One Python class per source under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors). [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md) is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real one against a free no-auth API, so you can follow it without a vendor account. Requests and votes live in the [connector wishlist (#356)](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues/356).
- **Write a hunt.** Hunt-as-Code YAML hypotheses under [`hunts/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/hunts); [Hello, hunt](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/detections/hello-hunt.md) walks through one.
- **Add a playbook** under [`playbooks/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/playbooks).
- **Fix a typo or improve a doc page** under [`apps/docs/docs/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/apps/docs/docs).

## Step 3 — Make the change, open a PR

Commits need a sign-off (`git commit -s`); `git commit --amend -s --no-edit` fixes the last one and `git rebase --signoff main` fixes a branch.

The default [pull-request template](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md) walks you through what we need. The eval-harness section is required for substrate, playbook and detection changes — tick "Not applicable" otherwise.

Two things worth knowing before your first PR, because they're enforced and they surprise people:

- **Every published claim has to be true.** If you add a link it must resolve, and if you state a number it has to come from the tree rather than from memory. CI checks a lot of this.
- **No mock or fabricated data in the authenticated product.** Seeded and synthetic data is gated behind demo mode and labelled; honest empty and error states are the default everywhere else.

If you get stuck, [open a Q&A discussion](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/discussions/new?category=q-a) — don't suffer in silence.

The full contributor guide is [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and **Your first 30 minutes** near the top of it is a four-step version of this page.

Looking forward to your first PR. 🛡️

issues.title: Connector wishlist — what should AiSOC ingest next?
issues.body:
This is the rolling wishlist for **new connectors** the community would like to see ingested by AiSOC.

## How to vote / request

- 👍 the top comment for a connector you want.
- Reply with the *exact* product name + source format (REST? JSONL? syslog? S3 export?) + a link to the vendor's API docs. A signal score helps prioritisation: how many enterprises already rely on this in their SOC?
- If you've already shipped a custom connector for AiSOC, drop it here — even unmerged forks help.

## How to *build* one

**Start with [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md)** ([on the docs site](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors/hello-connector)). It is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real, runnable connector against a free no-auth HTTP service, so you can walk every line of the contract — `schema()`, `test_connection()`, `fetch_alerts()`, `normalize()` and a smoke test — without a vendor account or an API key. [Connectors overview](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/index.md) is the companion reference.

Connectors live under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors), one Python class per source. The shape:

1. Subclass `BaseConnector` ([`base.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/base.py)) and declare a `schema()` returning a `ConnectorSchema` with the config fields your connector needs.
2. Pick a category. There are **nine**: `ai`, `cloud`, `edr`, `iam`, `ndr`, `network`, `saas`, `siem`, `vcs`.
3. Mark sensitive fields `secret=True` so the credential vault encrypts them at rest.
4. Register the class in `_CONNECTOR_CLASSES` **and `__all__`** in [`__init__.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py). Discovery is registry-based, so there is no other wiring — but two artefacts are derived from that tuple and both are `--check`-gated in CI, so regenerate and commit them or the build reds:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py   # the "N connectors" claims
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_types.py   # the console's ConnectorType union
   ```
5. Add a marketplace manifest at `plugins/<connector-id>/plugin.yaml` mirroring `schema()`, then run `pnpm marketplace:sync`.
6. Preserve all five severity tiers in `normalize()` — `info | low | medium | high | critical`. If the vendor publishes a distinct `critical`, map it to `critical`; do not collapse it into `high`.
7. Nest the vendor payload under `raw_event` (not `raw`). The ingest normalizer's canonical-envelope check keys on that, and a connector that gets it wrong falls through to the generic profile, which is how events end up archived but never promoted to alerts.

Per-connector documentation pages under `apps/docs/docs/connectors/` are **generated** by [`scripts/generate_connector_docs.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/scripts/generate_connector_docs.py), which also owns the `Connectors` list in [`apps/docs/sidebars.ts`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/sidebars.ts) between its `GENERATED CONNECTOR LIST` markers — so run the generator rather than hand-editing the sidebar. A hand-written page wins over the generated one, but it still has to mention every required and secret field; the generator appends a marker-wrapped field reference to enforce that.

## Currently most-requested (auto-curated from comments)

_Maintainers will edit this list as votes pile up. PRs always welcome — the issue tracker is just the queue._

| Source | Category | Status |
|--------|----------|--------|
| _comments below feed this table_ |        |        |

## What already ships

**87 connectors** out of the box: 22 SaaS, 18 cloud, 17 SIEM, 10 EDR, 7 IAM, 7 network, 3 VCS, 2 NDR, 1 AI. The count is derived from the registry by `python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py` and gated in CI, so check it there rather than trusting this paragraph.

The authoritative list is [`_CONNECTOR_CLASSES`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py) or the [connectors overview](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors). Not the marketplace — [`marketplace/index.json`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/marketplace/index.json) carries **77** plugin manifests against those 84 registered connectors, so it undercounts. (A missing manifest for your connector is itself a reasonable first PR.)

If your tool isn't in the catalog and you don't want to write code, **universal capture** may already cover it — webhook URLs, an email relay, CEF syslog and Splunk HEC let any vendor that can POST or send mail land events in the same OCSF stream.

issues.title: Reduce Benchmark Results payload with source-sharded, lazy-loaded registry
issues.body:
## Context

After PR #59, `data/benchmark-results.json` is approximately **70.8 MB**. The current `/results/` page fetches the complete JSON snapshot before it can populate filters or display the first page. This makes the benchmark explorer increasingly expensive to load and parse, especially as additional benchmark sources are added.

## Goal

Keep the source-linked, no-cross-suite-ranking policy while making the explorer scale with the dataset.

## Proposed design

1. **Small manifest**
   - Add a compact manifest containing schema/database version, import date, source metadata, per-source record counts and shard paths.
   - Do not include all result records in the manifest.

2. **Source-specific shards**
   - Split records into deterministic source shards (initially MLPerf Inference and InferenceX).
   - Preserve record IDs, original source keys, all workload/system/software provenance, raw metrics and normalized metric semantics.
   - Keep deterministic ordering and content hashes so refreshes are auditable.

3. **Lazy loading**
   - Load the manifest first and render source status immediately.
   - Load only the selected source shard; load all shards only when the user selects “All sources”.
   - Keep the existing filters, metric-direction sorting, pagination and source links working across loaded records.
   - Show per-source loading/error states and allow retry without discarding already loaded data.

4. **CI and data governance**
   - Validate manifest/shard consistency, record counts, unique IDs, source ownership and hashes.
   - Ensure the importer/refresh workflow writes the manifest and shards atomically.
   - Keep a migration test proving the sharded representation is semantically equivalent to the current monolithic registry.

## Acceptance criteria

- Initial page load transfers the manifest only, not the 70 MB full registry.
- Selecting one source fetches only that source's shard.
- “All sources” returns the same records and filter semantics as the current explorer.
- No record, metric, provenance field or comparability safeguard is lost.
- Existing browser smoke tests pass, with new tests for lazy loading, retries, source switching and manifest/shard integrity.
- The full monolithic file is no longer required for GitHub Pages runtime or normal refreshes.

## Non-goals

- No composite score or cross-suite leaderboard.
- No lossy compression or dropping raw publisher metrics.
- No changes to benchmark source interpretation or evidence levels.

## Related
- PR #59: automated refresh of the source-linked benchmark results registry.
- Current UI: `assets/js/benchmark-results.js`.
- Current importer: `scripts/import_benchmark_results.py`.

issues.title: Hacker News drops every hit for multi-word topics: `_title_matches_query` keeps the quote characters
issues.body:
**Version:** v4.6.0 (64b1f006), still present on `main` at 331025e6.

**What happens**

For any multi-word topic, the HN lane returns 0 stories. With topic `Claude Code`:

```
[HN] Searching for '"claude code"' (raw: '"Claude Code"', since 2026-10-24, count=15)
[HN] Found 15 stories
[HN] Prefix filter removed 15/15 false-positive hits for '"Claude Code"'
✓ Research complete (3.4s) - HN: 0 stories
```

**Cause**

`parse_hackernews_response` passes the quoted phrase to `_title_matches_query`. There,
`_flatten_query_for_algolia('"claude code"')` keeps the quotes, so the tokens become
`"claude` and `code"`. The pattern `\b"claude\b` needs a word character before the quote,
which a title never has, so no title matches and every hit is dropped.

```python
from lib import hackernews as h
h._title_matches_query('Claude Code now supports X', '"claude code"')  # False
h._title_matches_query('Claude Code now supports X', 'claude code')    # True
```

**Fix that worked locally**

```python
query_words = [w.strip('"') for w in _flatten_query_for_algolia(query.lower()).split() if w.strip('"')]
```

With this change the same run returns 6 HN stories, and `tests/test_hackernews.py` plus
`tests/test_hackernews_comment_floor.py` pass (166 tests). The short-token guard still holds
(`_title_matches_query('Email artists', '"ai ts"')` stays False).

issues.title: Marketplace counts formatted with the runtime's locale hydrate differently for visitors in another locale (React #418)
issues.body:
### What happens

Marketplace pages format counts with `toLocaleString()` and no locale, so the text depends on the runtime that formats it. The server renders with its own locale. A visitor whose browser uses a different one, such as German, renders the same count differently while hydrating: `1,234 runs` on the server, `1.234 runs` in the browser. For any count of 1,000 or more, React throws error #418, re-renders the page in the browser, and the error goes to Sentry.

This is the same class of bug as #17309 and #17310, with locale where those had clock skew. The route crawl (#17314) can't see it, because its browser and server share a locale.

### Where

In `autogpt_platform/frontend/src/app/(platform)/marketplace/`:
- `skills/[slug]/components/SkillPage.tsx` (installs)
- `components/AgentInfo/AgentInfo.tsx` (runs)
- `components/StoreCard/StoreCard.tsx`
- `components/FeaturedAgentCard/FeaturedAgentCard.tsx`
- `components/WorkflowsShelf/components/WorkflowTile.tsx`
- `components/SkillsSection/components/SkillCard.tsx`
- `components/Shelf/ShelfMoreButton.tsx`
- `skills/components/SkillsBrowsePage/SkillsBrowsePage.tsx`

`AgentInfo`'s changelog date already passes `"en-US"`, which is why it's safe.

### Expected

A server-rendered number or date reads the same on the server and while hydrating, whatever the visitor's locale.

### Possible fix

- Format with one fixed locale everywhere a value can render on the server, through a shared helper. Or switch to the visitor's locale only after mount, as `RelativeTime` does for times (#17331).
- Add a lint rule, like #17331's for relative times, that refuses a bare `toLocaleString()` or `toLocaleDateString()` without a locale.
- A route-crawl variant with a non-English browser locale (Playwright's `locale` option) would catch the class end to end.

issues.title: Running a block directly: blocks that need a graph run fail, graph-only blocks slip through the internal route, and invalid input is charged
issues.body:
Found while fixing #17321 (PR #17343). These are separate from credentials, and all of them exist on `dev` today.

### 1. Blocks that need a graph run fail when run directly

Some blocks aren't graph-only, yet their `run()` needs `graph_id`, `graph_exec_id` or `node_exec_id`. A direct run (`POST /api/blocks/{id}/execute`, or v1's `POST /blocks/{id}/execute`) doesn't have them, so it fails with a server error rather than a 4xx. They are:
- the four mem0 blocks;
- Persist Information and Retrieve Information;
- Video Clip, Video Concat and Video Narration.

**Expected:** either such a block refuses a direct run up front with a 4xx that says why, or the direct run supplies what it needs.

### 2. The internal route runs graph-only blocks

v1's route refuses graph-only blocks, but the internal `POST /api/blocks/{id}/execute` lets them through.

**Expected:** both routes apply the same rule.

### 3. A direct run is charged before its inputs are validated

A direct run charges for the block, then validates the non-credential inputs. A request with invalid input is therefore charged for a run that never happens. The graph executor never charges a node that fails input validation.

**Expected:** validate first, then charge, as the executor does.

issues.body:
Refs #775 and #801. Local triage of 77 archive records previously blocked by DXC timeouts recovered DXIL for 63 with -Od. WARP created pipelines for those 63 after a separate host-stack diagnostic. RTX still showed time and memory limits. This issue covers cross-adapter mesh pipeline measurements.

Claim an adapter and driver in a comment. Use a source-built mesh shader with known output and a generated stress variant that preserves that output. Identify the source revision, target profile and tools. Compile the same input with default optimization and -Od. Where both compile, feed each exact DXIL blob into the same PSO harness with identical descriptors and pipeline state. Compare WARP and at least one physical adapter. Reports for additional vendors are welcome.

- Record DXC version, flags, compile time and outcome separately from pipeline time, peak process memory and outcome. Include the adapter, driver, Windows build and debug-layer status.
- Distinguish unsupported mesh capability, compiler diagnostics, time or memory limits, driver/process exit and returned HRESULT. Report any changed watchdog, memory or host stack setting as a separate run.

issues.title: [Feature]: OpenViking SuperAgent 支持钉钉 Stream 群聊接入
issues.body:
### Issue Origin

Observed or reproduced in a real environment（已在真实环境中验证）。

### Problem Statement

我在自己的环境中部署了 OpenViking SuperAgent，希望能从钉钉群里直接使用它。目前 SuperAgent 的 Connector 配置缺少钉钉渠道，因此钉钉群无法作为同一个 SuperAgent 实例的消息入口。

### Proposed Solution

为 SuperAgent 增加可选的 `dingtalk` Connector。首版以自建应用所属组织的内部群为范围，接收群里 @ 机器人的文本消息，转换为 SuperAgent 标准事件，复用现有的任务调度和定时器。任务结果和到期提醒通过钉钉群消息 API 发回原群，使用 Markdown 发送。

接收端先把事件持久化到实例本地 SQLite，再向钉钉发送 ACK。向 Core 转发发生异常时自动退避重试。成功写出事件后保留 24 小时，用于重启重放。Core 按 Connector 实例和事件 ID 去重，并应用现有的消息时效规则。钉钉 ACK 对应本地 SQLite 持久化，当前 Connector 协议没有 Core 落库回执。

### Alternatives Considered

仓库中的 VikingBot 已有钉钉渠道，可用于 VikingBot 的群聊交互。本需求面向 SuperAgent，目标是让钉钉群直接复用当前实例的工作区、Worker 工单和定时器。

### Feature Area

Other — OpenViking SuperAgent / IM Connector。

### Use Case

在钉钉群里 @ SuperAgent，请它分析工作区的源码并把结果发回本群。也可以在群里发起定时提醒，触发时由机器人主动在原群发送。

实例配置示例（节选）：

```json
{
  "channel": "lark",
  "connectors": ["lark", "dingtalk"]
}
```

钉钉作为企业内部群聊渠道接入。主 IM 保持为已绑定 owner 的渠道，负责主动通知、邮件审批和主渠道管理。钉钉应用凭证保存在实例私有数据目录，可用 `ov-superagent login dingtalk [instance]` 更新。

### Additional Context

原连接器版本已在真实钉钉群验证了 @ 消息接收、原群回复、到期提醒和 Worker 结果回传。Daemon 重启后，两条测试事件都被重放，Core 各保留一条入库记录，原群消息发送次数保持不变。修订后的实现和测试命令见 PR #8178。

### 首版范围与投递边界

1. **首版范围**覆盖自建应用所在组织的内部群。机器人接收明确 @ 自己的文本，在原群发送 Markdown 回复和定时提醒。支持 owner 私聊的主 IM 继续处理主动通知和邮件审批。
2. **确认边界**为有效事件先提交到 Connector 本地 SQLite，再向钉钉 ACK。写入 Worker 输出管道后保留 24 小时，用于重启重放。Core 独立执行消息时效判定和去重。当前协议缺少 Core 持久化回执，端到端交付仍取决于 Core 入库和后续执行。协议级回执可以作为后续增强。

### Contribution

- [x] I am willing to contribute to implementing this feature

issues.title: S3: PutBucketVersioning accepts Suspended on a bucket with Object Lock
issues.body:
A bucket created with Object Lock enabled can have its versioning suspended. AWS refuses with `409 InvalidBucketState` and the bucket stays `Enabled`, since a lock protects object versions.

In an earlier run that suspended the bucket first, a later `CompleteMultipartUpload` into it returned no `VersionId`.

One script, run twice: once against real AWS S3 in `us-east-1` and once against MiniStack v1.5.43 (`ministackorg/ministack:1.5.43`), asked directly. The only difference between the two runs is the endpoint argument. The client is boto3 with botocore 1.44.4 for both. The whole script is at the bottom, and both transcripts are from that run.

The bucket is created with `ObjectLockEnabledForBucket=True`.

**AWS**

```
PutBucketVersioning Suspended                        409 InvalidBucketState
GetBucketVersioning                                  Enabled
```

**MiniStack**

```
PutBucketVersioning Suspended                        200
GetBucketVersioning                                  Suspended
```

## The script

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Suspending versioning on a bucket with S3 Object Lock.
    python3 suspend.py                         # real AWS, us-east-1
    python3 suspend.py http://127.0.0.1:4566   # MiniStack
"""
import datetime, sys, time
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config
from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

endpoint = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
s3 = boto3.client('s3', region_name='us-east-1', endpoint_url=endpoint,
                  config=Config(retries={'max_attempts': 1}))
stamp = str(int(time.time()))
DST = 'lock-' + stamp
UNTIL = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0) + datetime.timedelta(days=1)

def show(label, f, **kw):
    try:
        r = f(**kw)
        print('%-52s %s' % (label, r['ResponseMetadata']['HTTPStatusCode']))
        return r
    except ClientError as e:
        print('%-52s %s %s' % (label, e.response['ResponseMetadata']['HTTPStatusCode'], e.response['Error']['Code']))

def lock_state(label, bucket, key):
    h = s3.head_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=key)
    print('%-52s mode=%s until=%s legal-hold=%s' % (label, h.get('ObjectLockMode'),
          'set' if h.get('ObjectLockRetainUntilDate') else None, h.get('ObjectLockLegalHoldStatus')))

def cleanup(bucket):
    try:
        v = s3.list_object_versions(Bucket=bucket)
    except ClientError:
        return
    for o in v.get('Versions', []) + v.get('DeleteMarkers', []):
        try:
            s3.put_object_legal_hold(Bucket=bucket, Key=o['Key'], VersionId=o['VersionId'], LegalHold={'Status': 'OFF'})
        except ClientError:
            pass
        s3.delete_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=o['Key'], VersionId=o['VersionId'], BypassGovernanceRetention=True)
    for u in s3.list_multipart_uploads(Bucket=bucket).get('Uploads', []):
        s3.abort_multipart_upload(Bucket=bucket, Key=u['Key'], UploadId=u['UploadId'])
    s3.delete_bucket(Bucket=bucket)

s3.create_bucket(Bucket=DST, ObjectLockEnabledForBucket=True)
try:
    show('PutBucketVersioning Suspended', s3.put_bucket_versioning, Bucket=DST,
         VersioningConfiguration={'Status': 'Suspended'})
    print('%-52s %s' % ('GetBucketVersioning', s3.get_bucket_versioning(Bucket=DST).get('Status')))
finally:
    cleanup(DST)
```

issues.title: stepfunctions: an execution started on a version ARN runs the latest definition, not the version's
issues.body:
### Summary

`StartExecution` with a state machine **version** ARN (`...:stateMachine:name:1`) runs the state machine's current definition instead of that version's, and `DescribeExecution` omits `stateMachineVersionArn`. On AWS, a version is immutable and an execution started on its ARN runs the version's definition; `DescribeExecution` reports the version ARN.

In `stepfunctions.py`, `_start_execution` resolves the version ARN to the base machine (`_resolve_state_machine_arn`) and stores only that, and `_run_execution` loads `_state_machines[execution["stateMachineArn"]]["definition"]`. `_execution_version_arn` already finds the version, and `_state_machine_versions` already stores each version's `definition`; it is used today only for the execution's `encryptionConfiguration`.

### Reproduce (MiniStack 1.5.43)

```sh
aws stepfunctions create-state-machine --name repro --role-arn arn:aws:iam::000000000000:role/r --publish \
  --definition '{"StartAt":"P","States":{"P":{"Type":"Pass","Result":"v1","End":true}}}'
# -> stateMachineVersionArn ...:stateMachine:repro:1
aws stepfunctions update-state-machine --state-machine-arn arn:aws:states:us-east-1:000000000000:stateMachine:repro --publish \
  --definition '{"StartAt":"P","States":{"P":{"Type":"Pass","Result":"v2","End":true}}}'
# -> ...:stateMachine:repro:2
aws stepfunctions start-execution --state-machine-arn arn:aws:states:us-east-1:000000000000:stateMachine:repro:1
aws stepfunctions describe-execution --execution-arn <executionArn>
```

**Actual:** `"output": "\"v2\""`, and no `stateMachineVersionArn` in the response.

**Expected:** `"output": "\"v1\""`, and `"stateMachineVersionArn": "arn:aws:states:us-east-1:000000000000:stateMachine:repro:1"`.

### Evidence it holds on AWS

- The botocore model documents `DescribeExecutionOutput.stateMachineVersionArn` as "the state machine version associated with the execution ... If you start an execution from a StartExecution request without specifying a state machine version or alias ARN, Step Functions returns a null value", and `StartExecutionInput.stateMachineArn` accepts a version ARN as the thing to execute.
- Our execution suite starts an instance on version 1 after version 2 is published, asserts `DescribeExecution.stateMachineVersionArn` is version 1's ARN and that the run follows version 1's definition. It passes on AWS and fails on MiniStack.

### Use case

Workflows keep running the template version they were started from while newer versions are published. Related to #2770 (`UpdateStateMachine` omits `revisionId` unless `publish`).

issues.title: S3: UploadPartCopy accepts another key's upload ID
issues.body:
`UploadPartCopy` accepts an upload ID that belongs to another key and adds the part to that other key's upload. AWS answers `404 NoSuchUpload`, as it does for `UploadPart`, and leaves the upload untouched.

MiniStack already refuses the same mismatch on `UploadPart`, so only the copy path is affected.

One script, run twice: once against real AWS S3 in `us-east-1` and once against MiniStack v1.5.43 (`ministackorg/ministack:1.5.43`), asked directly. The only difference between the two runs is the endpoint argument. The client is boto3 with botocore 1.44.4 for both. The whole script is at the bottom, and both transcripts are from that run.

The upload is created for key `a`; both part requests name key `b` with that upload ID.

**AWS**

```
CreateMultipartUpload for key a
UploadPart 1 to key b with a's upload ID                     404 NoSuchUpload
UploadPartCopy 2 to key b with a's upload ID                 404 NoSuchUpload
ListParts of key a's upload                                  []
```

**MiniStack**

```
CreateMultipartUpload for key a
UploadPart 1 to key b with a's upload ID                     404 NoSuchUpload
UploadPartCopy 2 to key b with a's upload ID                 200
ListParts of key a's upload                                  [2]
```

## The script

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""UploadPart and UploadPartCopy naming another key's upload ID.
    python3 partcopy.py                         # real AWS, us-east-1
    python3 partcopy.py http://127.0.0.1:4566   # MiniStack
"""
import sys, time
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config
from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

endpoint = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
s3 = boto3.client('s3', region_name='us-east-1', endpoint_url=endpoint,
                  config=Config(retries={'max_attempts': 1}))
BUCKET = 'part-key-' + str(int(time.time()))

def show(label, f, **kw):
    try:
        r = f(**kw)
        print('%-60s %s' % (label, r['ResponseMetadata']['HTTPStatusCode']))
        return r
    except ClientError as e:
        print('%-60s %s %s' % (label, e.response['ResponseMetadata']['HTTPStatusCode'], e.response['Error']['Code']))

def parts(label, key, upload_id):
    try:
        r = s3.list_parts(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=key, UploadId=upload_id)
        print('%-60s %s' % (label, [p['PartNumber'] for p in r.get('Parts', [])]))
    except ClientError as e:
        print('%-60s %s %s' % (label, e.response['ResponseMetadata']['HTTPStatusCode'], e.response['Error']['Code']))

s3.create_bucket(Bucket=BUCKET)
try:
    s3.put_object(Bucket=BUCKET, Key='source', Body=b'source')
    upload_id = s3.create_multipart_upload(Bucket=BUCKET, Key='a')['UploadId']
    print('CreateMultipartUpload for key a')
    show('UploadPart 1 to key b with a\'s upload ID', s3.upload_part, Bucket=BUCKET, Key='b',
         UploadId=upload_id, PartNumber=1, Body=b'part')
    show('UploadPartCopy 2 to key b with a\'s upload ID', s3.upload_part_copy, Bucket=BUCKET, Key='b',
         UploadId=upload_id, PartNumber=2, CopySource={'Bucket': BUCKET, 'Key': 'source'})
    parts('ListParts of key a\'s upload', 'a', upload_id)
finally:
    for u in s3.list_multipart_uploads(Bucket=BUCKET).get('Uploads', []):
        s3.abort_multipart_upload(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=u['Key'], UploadId=u['UploadId'])
    for o in s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket=BUCKET).get('Contents', []):
        s3.delete_object(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=o['Key'])
    s3.delete_bucket(Bucket=BUCKET)
```

issues.title: CI: ChatPageDrafts prefill test fails on main once its pinned clock is 30 days old
issues.body:
[operator: bolichen97]

### What happens

`Frontend Tests (3)` fails on `main` and on every PR whose run includes the full frontend suite:

```
 FAIL  src/test/ChatPageDrafts.test.tsx > ChatPage draft persistence > leaves the draft alone when a staged prefill belongs to another slot
AssertionError: expected '' to be 'mine, still here' // Object.is equality
 Test Files  1 failed | 1185 passed (1186)
```

First red run on main: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/45033349268/job/137244551113 (47f3ff3c88). The same node id is red on #40810, #40812, #40816 and #40636.

No commit broke it. The test file last changed in #36727, and the test fails on every run started after 2026-11-22 14:00 UTC.

### Cause

Earlier tests in the same file pin `Date.now` to `2026-10-23T14:00:00Z` (`TAKE_BACK_NOW`) and write a `slot-a` draft while it is pinned. The chat-draft store (`createSlotDraftStore` in `website/src/utils/slotDraftStore.ts`) keeps each slot's last-touched time in module memory. The file's `beforeEach` clears `localStorage`, but not that in-memory map.

So the failing test loads its `slot-a` draft with the stamp an earlier test left at `2026-10-23T14:00:00Z`. Once the real clock passed that time plus the 30-day draft TTL (2026-11-22 14:00 UTC), the store prunes the draft as expired and the composer comes up empty.

### Expected

`ChatPageDrafts.test.tsx` resets the chat-draft store between tests (the store already exports `__resetForTests`), so each test reads only the drafts it wrote, whatever today's date is.

issues.title: WeCom inbound media downloads ignore NO_PROXY, unlike the client's reply and WebSocket
issues.body:
### Existing issues

- [x] I searched open issues and this is not already reported.

### KiroCrew version

Source checkout of `main` at `e3c76363`

### Release channel

Nightly (source checkout of `main`)

### How is it installed?

From source

### Platform

Not platform-specific

### What happened

#40488 made the WeCom client's reply POST and WebSocket go directly to a host listed in `NO_PROXY`. Its Not a goal section left out "WeCom's attachment-ingest session", and nothing tracks that gap. `wecom.media.download_media` still sends every inbound media URL through the single proxy resolved at startup (`session.get(vetted.url, proxy=proxy, ...)`), whatever `NO_PROXY` says.

Suppose the proxy refuses the WeCom media CDN but the CDN is reachable directly, and the operator lists it in `NO_PROXY`. The channel connects and text works, but every inbound picture or file fails with `media download failed`. Bypassing the proxy would also put the fetch on the address-pinned session that the SSRF vet sets up. That pin is skipped whenever a proxy is used.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
NO_PROXY=cdn.example python -c "
import asyncio, aiohttp
from kiro_crew import link_unfurl
from kiro_crew.wecom import media
link_unfurl._default_resolve = lambda *a: ['93.184.216.34']
class S:
    def get(self, url, **kw): print('proxied via', kw.get('proxy')); raise aiohttp.ClientError()
try: asyncio.run(media.download_media(S(), 'https://cdn.example/o', 'A'*43, proxy='http://proxy.example:3128'))
except Exception as e: print(e)"
```

It prints `proxied via http://proxy.example:3128`.

### Expected

A media host listed in `NO_PROXY` is fetched directly, the way the client's other requests are.

### Proposed fix

`download_media` passes the proxy through `http_proxy.proxy_for_url(proxy, vetted.url)`. A bypassed host then takes the existing address-pinned direct session. I have a fix with regression tests ready and will open the PR.
