issues.title: tests: pixel_aot draws spend most of their time creating a D3D12 device per case
issues.body:
_AI-assisted (Claude Code). Measurements from my own machine._

### Problem

`pixel_aot_check.py draw` launches `offscreen_check.exe` once per case, and each launch creates a new D3D12 device. That device creation dominates the test time, and new draws keep adding to it. `pixel_aot_hardware` has `TIMEOUT 60`.

At `3f02f4d`, Windows 10 22H2 (19045.7846), RTX 3080 Ti (driver 32.0.16.1047), debug layer enabled, DXC 1.9.2609.5, idle machine:

| | `pixel_aot_hardware` | `pixel_aot_warp` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total | 46.5 s | 11.1 s |
| `offscreen_check.exe`, 134 launches | 44.0 s | 8.4 s |
| `dxc.exe`, 56 calls | 1.9 s | 2.1 s |
| Python | 0.6 s | 0.6 s |

A program that only creates a hardware device and a queue takes 300–360 ms per process; the debug layer adds about 10–30 ms. Under moderate background load the hardware test took 57–60 s and timed out in 4 of 5 runs.

### Proposal

An opt-in `offscreen_check <backend> --batch <file>` that creates the device once and runs the listed cases on it, printing the same per-case output and status as today. The single-case command line stays unchanged.

This touches the same `main()` as #166 (operation table, explicit pass/77/fail). It could build on top of #166 once that lands: device setup once, then one table row per case.

Two PRs, after #166:

1. `offscreen_check` batch mode and its controls.
2. `pixel_aot_check.py` switches to it, timed to avoid the open `pixel_aot` PRs.

Estimated result: hardware under 10 s, WARP about 4 s.

### Alternatives

- Raise `TIMEOUT`: simple, but the test keeps growing.
- Split `pixel_aot_*` into several tests: shorter tests, same total time.
- Keep one process per case: it isolates crashes and device state, which the batch mode must preserve.

### Verification

On WARP and hardware:

- A batch gives the same output and status per case as separate runs.
- A `pixel_mismatch` case between passing cases fails alone.
- Debug-layer errors are attributed to the case that caused them.
- After a forced device removal, every remaining case fails.
- The exit status is non-zero if any case failed.

Is one process per case intentional, for example to isolate driver state? If so, would you prefer a higher timeout instead?

### Checklist

- [x] I checked for an existing issue or pull request for this change.
- [x] I did not include game files, dumps, distribution links or credentials.

issues.title: [Research] Audit atmospheric propagation and model mismatch before production changes
issues.body:
User-requested isolated falsification study. Atmospheric propagation has a separate owner from discovery, association, confidence, context validation and product integration. Do not refactor production code or tune the current reference cases.

Use frozen aircraft trajectories and independently rendered acoustic fixtures to vary direction-dependent wind and vertical temperature/wind profiles. Run the existing localization model unchanged. Compare localization displacement, association changes, and accepted/inconclusive outcomes at 100, 500 and 1,000 m, retaining every selected case and any missing-ray/numerical failure.

Establish the independent propagation solver against analytic still-air/uniform-flow limits and numerical convergence checks before attributing localization changes to weather. Source realistic profile ranges from primary meteorological/acoustics references, distinguish constant sound-speed variation from advection/refraction, and state omitted effects and the scope of any bounds. Keep truth outside search inputs; post-run evaluation only.

Deliver a reproducible, source-pinned error budget stating whether effects are negligible within the tested domain, conservatively bounded, or material enough to justify a separate weather-informed implementation task. Preserve inputs, hashes, negative cases, runtime and complete results. An inconclusive product decision is not a successful location, and a best-ranked coordinate shift is a different metric.

Default coordination: discussion board #39. Current target: up to 1 km acceptable, 100–500 m or better preferred. A 3/4/6-event independent emission-domain fixture generator is being published on agent/multi-event-fixture-20261103; reuse frozen trajectories where suitable, but atmospheric waveform synthesis must be independent of production acoustic/Doppler code. No source YouTube MP4.

issues.title: [Research] Audit recording robustness and measure failure thresholds before corrections
issues.body:
User-requested isolated recording robustness audit. Unclaimed until the user deploys a worker; do not launch a subagent. Keep production discovery/matching/decision code frozen. Report failure thresholds before proposing new correction models.

Use independently rendered fixtures plus eligible real field recordings when available. Freeze baseline inputs/model/configuration and a bounded test matrix before inspecting outcomes. Keep original truth hidden from search and retain every transformation, failure and inconclusive case.

Audit dimensions:
1. Phone processing: measured paired-device exports or actual device recordings for AGC, denoising, beamforming and other documented processing. Label simulated processing as synthetic; do not equate a generic filter with a particular phone.
2. Compression/resampling: MP3/AAC/Opus profiles, bitrate/sample-rate changes, encoder-delay/gapless metadata, clipping and repeated encoding. Independently measure timing offsets/drift as well as spectral loss.
3. Wind noise at the microphone: controlled mixtures or paired field measurements across a declared SNR range. Direction-dependent atmospheric advection/refraction belongs to #49 and is not duplicated here.
4. Reverberation: documented measured or synthetic impulse responses across a declared decay range. Record direct-path delay and processing order; distinguish illustrative stress cases from measured environments.
5. Microphone movement: independently generated receiver trajectories or measured motion with reference GPS/IMU. Define the reference time/location and motion footprint before evaluation; do not select whichever point on a path makes the error smallest. Static-recorder assumptions may properly lead to abstention.
6. Playback-rate/sample-clock changes: fixed rate errors and drift, including small fractional changes. Preserve the intended time mapping and measure how errors affect Doppler timing/frequency; do not silently correct the pipeline in the audit.

For every selected baseline/perturbation report detection recall/false proposals where labels exist, matched independent-event count, flight-association changes, location error and displacement at 100/500/1,000 m, actual decision/abstention, unsupported accepted fixes, runtime and input/code/transform hashes. Distinguish best-ranked coordinates from accepted estimates and avoid calling missing clock/coverage a recording-processing failure.

Deliver reproducible scripts/configuration and a documented error budget with dose-response/failure ranges, interaction limits and all negative results. Do not generalize one source's threshold to all recordings. If a material failure needs correction, open a focused evidence-based implementation task; otherwise close the investigation without adding complexity.

Dependencies/coordination: field-corpus acquisition (new P0 task), evaluator #3, final acceptance #13, atmospheric audit #49 and discussion board #39. Use the primary's frozen 3/4/6-event generator when suitable; do not create competing production ownership. Preserve historical experiments and exclude the source YouTube MP4.

issues.title: [High / Data integrity] Independently audit historical aircraft passages across ADS-B archives
issues.body:
## Objective
Measure whether changing between legitimate independent historical flight-data sources materially changes inferred location, flight association or confidence/abstention. This is an external data-validation study and error-budget contribution, not another ingestion feature.

## Ownership and boundaries
Available for a USER-deployed data-audit worker, separate from W2 acquisition/index implementation. Claim scope/files on Discussion #39. Own source provenance, immutable comparison fixtures, audit scripts and reports; use frozen existing adapters or isolated audit converters. Coordinate any production format/interface request with W2. No production interpolation/model tuning during the initial study; no subagents.

## Protocol
1. Identify two genuinely independent ADS-B archives with overlapping real aircraft passages/time windows. Document collection provenance, possible common upstream feeds, access/licence limitations, identifier mapping, raw hashes and exclusions. Two mirrors of the same underlying traces are not independent measurements. If eligible second-source data are unavailable, report exactly what is missing; do not substitute a synthetic comparison and call it complete.
2. Select passages and matching tolerances independently of which source yields a better localization. Freeze a common recording, acoustic detections/settings, terrain, recording-time window, search scope, scoring/decision code and budgets. Keep evaluation coordinates out of backend inputs.
3. Compare raw timestamp semantics/resolution and clock offsets, horizontal positions, velocity, altitude fields and datum/provenance, cadence, duplicate observations, dropouts and segment gaps. Never silently compare pressure altitude with geometric/ellipsoidal height. Report unresolved datum conversions explicitly.
4. Preserve native observations. A common-epoch interpolation comparison must declare interpolation/support rules and must not bridge unsupported gaps or erase the native differences. Separate identity-association mistakes from actual cross-source measurement discrepancies.
5. Run matched complete localization replays differing only in the legitimate flight-data source. Also report common-support controls separately from each archive's real missing-data coverage; do not quietly drop inconvenient passages or constrain a search using truth.

## Deliverables / completion evidence
- Source-pinned raw/derived manifests, comparison script and reproducible source-swap replay configuration.
- Per-passage and aggregate timestamp/position/altitude/gap discrepancies, plus complete association, location and decision outcomes for BOTH sources, including all failures.
- Location displacement, independently referenced errors at100/500/1000m where eligible, retained alternatives, runtime/memory, and accepted-to-inconclusive/flight-association transitions.
- A documented data-source error budget: negligible within the tested scope, conservatively bounded, or materially unmodelled. State sample limits and reference uncertainty. If material, propose an evidence-based follow-up requirement instead of tuning reference cases or unilaterally widening confidence.

Independent field corpus remains #53's collection scope; W4 owns evaluator semantics. Refs #6, #7, #9, #13. Discuss dependencies/results on #39. No source YouTube MP4 uploads.

issues.title: [Medium / Product] Give evidence-based next steps for inconclusive analyses
issues.body:
## Objective
Help a local application user understand what additional information could resolve an inconclusive analysis, using the actual retained evidence. Extend machine-readable reasons with inspectable next-step guidance; generic friendlier error text alone does not complete this task.

## Ownership
Available for a USER-deployed product/evidence worker. Coordinate on Discussion #39 with W5 (jobs/API/UI) and W4 (decision semantics). Own an additive guidance producer, focused checks and documentation; agree any shared-contract extension before coding. Preserve current status/reason_code and actual alternatives. Do not launch subagents.

## Required behavior
- Distinguish ambiguous distant locations/flight associations, insufficient independent events, uncertain recording start, unavailable/partial historical coverage, weak acoustic evidence, and exhausted computation. Each recommendation cites the diagnostics that justify it.
- Examples: request a defensible narrower recording-start window when retained modes differ in clock; suggest more of the ORIGINAL recording/another independent flyover when additional event evidence could distinguish distant modes; explain known archive coverage gaps when missing data prevent assessment; offer a budget/resume step only for an actually incomplete search.
- If two distant regions remain consistent with the evidence, explain that ambiguity using retained mode separation and association/time differences. Do not present one as the user's location or imply that more recording is guaranteed to fix it.
- Order recommendations only when measured diagnostics or a bounded counterfactual assessment supports the ordering. Distinguish an observed constraint from a suggestion whose benefit is unmeasured. Do not claim a calibrated probability or guaranteed error reduction.
- Any counterfactual uses frozen model/settings and the same competitor population; preserve unsupported alternatives and actual work limits. Do not rerun selectively until an attractive answer appears, manufacture timestamps or request ground-truth coordinates/known flight IDs as normal product inputs.
- Keep technical details in inspectable artifacts. User-facing advice should be concise, concrete and explain why that input is useful.

## Verification / deliverable
1. Publish the agreed additive guidance representation with evidence references, reason and recommendation limits; keep result validation and existing consumers compatible.
2. Exercise actual completed job artifacts for each supported reason, including missing-clock/coverage, distant near ties, few events and exhausted search. Verify every displayed recommendation is supported by that job's evidence.
3. Include a positive control where a legitimately narrower time window or additional independent event changes the competing-mode result, and a negative control where it does not. Preserve before/after outcomes; abstention remains valid.
4. Verify API serialization and real UI readback at desktop/mobile widths. Guidance must not change scores, acceptance thresholds or job status, nor hide alternatives.
5. Document remaining unmeasured benefits and provide replay commands/evidence hashes.

Refs #9, #10, #11, #13. This is separate from #54 recording robustness and the new end-to-end invariance audit; discuss overlapping files with their owners.

issues.title: [BUG] MCP client drops tools when tools/list response is paginated
issues.body:
### Description of Bug
In `integrations/mcp_client.py` and `integrations/github/mcp.py`, tool discovery via MCP executes a single `session.list_tools()` call:
```python
async def _list_tools_async(
    config: McpClientConfig,
    **session_options: Unpack[McpSessionOptions],
) -> list[types.Tool]:
    async with open_mcp_session(config, **session_options) as session:
        return list((await session.list_tools()).tools)
```
According to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification, `tools/list` responses are paginated via `nextCursor` / `next_cursor` on `ListToolsResult` and `PaginatedRequestParams(cursor=...)` on requests.

When connecting to an MCP server that paginates its tool roster across multiple pages:
1. `_list_tools_async` only returns the first page's tools; tools on subsequent pages (`next_cursor`) are silently dropped.
2. In `integrations/github/mcp.py`, `_validate_github_mcp_config_async` inspects tools on a single `await session.list_tools()`. If required repository tools or `get_me` are on page 2+, validation erroneously fails with `insufficient_tools`.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Connect an MCP server exposing 25+ tools that paginates with `nextCursor`.
2. Call `list_mcp_tools(config)`.
3. Notice only page 1 tools are returned; page 2+ tools are missing.

### Expected Behavior
`list_all_tools_on_session` should follow `next_cursor` using `PaginatedRequestParams(cursor=cursor)` until all pages are retrieved.

### Actual Behavior
Only the first page of tools is returned, dropping all remaining tools from discovery.

issues.title: [BUG] Persisted debug system prompts suppress conversation message history on session flush
issues.body:
### Description of Bug
In `core/agent_harness/session/persistence/jsonl_store.py` (and sister module `core/agent_harness/session/persistence/memory.py`), `flush()` checks whether the session's conversational messages in `session.agent.messages` need to be persisted:
```python
if session.agent.messages and not any(rec.get("type") == "message" for rec in records):
    for role, content in session.agent.messages:
        self.append_message(
            session.session_id,
            role=role,
            content=content,
            metadata={"kind": "chat"},
        )
```
During turn execution, `persist_turn_system_prompt()` (`infrastructure/observability/trace/prompts.py`) appends a diagnostic system prompt to the session store with `type="message"`, `role="system"`, and `metadata={"kind": phase, "debug": "system_prompt"}`.

Because the debug prompt record has `type="message"`, `not any(rec.get("type") == "message" for rec in records)` evaluates to `False`. As a result, the loop that flushes `session.agent.messages` is skipped, permanently dropping all conversation user and assistant messages from the persistent JSONL store and memory store upon session termination.

### Steps to Reproduce
```python
from core.agent_harness.session import InMemorySessionStore
from infrastructure.observability.trace.prompts import persist_turn_system_prompt
from surfaces.interactive_shell.session import Session

session = Session(store=InMemorySessionStore())
session.store.open_session(session)
session.agent.messages = [("user", "hello"), ("assistant", "world")]

persist_turn_system_prompt(session, phase="action_agent", system_prompt="system prompt")
session.store.flush(session)

records = session.store.read(session.session_id)
# Only the debug system prompt is in records; user and assistant messages were dropped.
assert not any(r.get("role") in ("user", "assistant") for r in records if r.get("type") == "message")
```

### Expected Behavior
`flush()` should check for existing non-debug conversation messages (ignoring diagnostic `debug="system_prompt"` records) and persist `session.agent.messages` so conversation history is not lost.

### Actual Behavior
`session.agent.messages` is completely dropped from disk/memory on session flush when a debug system prompt has been recorded.

issues.title: [FEATURE] GreptimeDB integration: SQL and PromQL over logs, traces, and metrics
issues.body:
### Problem statement

OpenSRE can't query GreptimeDB, so teams that send their OpenTelemetry data there can't use it for investigations.

[GreptimeDB](https://github.com/GreptimeTeam/greptimedb) is an open-source (Apache 2.0) observability database. It accepts OTLP metrics, logs, and traces and stores each signal as a table that you query with SQL or PromQL.

Because all three signals live in one database, one SQL query can join a span with its logs by `trace_id`. The other observability integrations in OpenSRE expose one tool per signal, and the agent has to merge their results itself.

The following query runs against the public demo at https://live.greptime.cloud/. That instance runs GreptimeDB v1.3.1, and the [OpenTelemetry Demo](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo) writes telemetry to it continuously. Open it in a browser and paste the query into **Table Query**:

```sql
SELECT t.service_name, t.span_name, l.severity_text, l.body
FROM opentelemetry_traces t
JOIN opentelemetry_logs l
  ON t.trace_id = l.trace_id AND t.span_id = l.span_id
WHERE t.timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
  AND l.timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
  AND l.severity_text = 'ERROR'
ORDER BY l.timestamp DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

### Proposed solution

Add `integrations/greptimedb/` with the same layout as SigNoz: config, client, setup, verifier, and tools.

Tools:

- `query_greptimedb_sql`: runs read-only SQL through the HTTP API (`/v1/sql`).
  - Accepts a single `SELECT`, `WITH`, `SHOW`, `DESC`, `EXPLAIN`, or `TQL` statement. The HTTP API executes every statement in a multi-statement body, so the tool rejects multi-statement input.
  - Sets a server-side timeout with `X-Greptime-Timeout`, caps returned rows with a `truncated` flag, and bounds the response size.
  - The statement check prevents accidental writes. The actual guarantee is a database user with `ReadOnly` permission, which the docs will recommend. A `ReadOnly` user gets HTTP 403 on DDL.
- `query_greptimedb_promql`: runs a Prometheus-compatible `query_range`.

The rest of the change:

- Setup through `opensre integrations setup greptimedb`. The verifier runs a real query.
- A docs page under `docs/integrations/monitoring/`.
- Unit tests that use responses captured from a real GreptimeDB.
- An E2E test that seeds correlated OTLP traces, logs, and metrics into a local standalone container and runs the join through the tool.

Out of scope: a tool `SKILL.md`, and the Jaeger- and Loki-compatible query APIs.

I work on GreptimeDB and can implement and maintain the integration. Does this fit the project's plans for integrations?

Neither dependency installation nor analytics installs it implicitly.

The missing command, after dependencies are installed, is:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python .github/ci/install_hooks.py
```

**2. Required persistence reference was deleted**

[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Tracer-Cloud/opensre/blob/29d9ba64ffe3d19abf1e02d0b8f711106a565a87/AGENTS.md#L94-L103) directs persistence/migration work to `PERSISTENCE.md`. The stale prerequisite must be reconciled with current guidance; this report does not request restoring the superseded document.

### Steps to reproduce and validation

2. Follow the persistence link in `AGENTS.md`, or run `test -e PERSISTENCE.md` from the checkout root; the command exits with status 1.
3. Existing hook-preservation and worktree-isolation tests passed during verification.

These discrepancies are platform-independent; inspection and tests were performed on macOS.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add the explicit hook installer to both no-Make recipes after dependencies are available.
- [ ] Preserve existing user hooks and checkout/worktree isolation.
- [ ] Link current maintained persistence guidance, or remove the obsolete required-reading row.
- [ ] Verify any replacement link resolves.
- [ ] Keep validation policy aligned with `CI.md`; no new checks or restored obsolete document are required.

Related history: #6638 proposed the setup correction but closed without merging. Detailed original persistence report: #7080.

issues.title: An old worker that outlives `hermes update` lazily imports a new-tree module that needs a name its loaded sibling lacks (`release_replaced_skill_view`)
issues.body:
## Summary

A process started on the old release keeps running across `hermes update` (here: a kanban worker held
busy while the gateway handoff waits for it). After the checkout moves, the first tool call of that
process imports `agent.tool_executor` **lazily** (`agent/lazy_forward.py` → `importlib.import_module`),
so Python reads the **new** `agent/tool_executor.py` from disk. Line 64 of the new file is

```python
from tools.skills_tool_dedup import release_replaced_skill_view, release_replaced_skill_views
```

but the process already holds the **old** `tools.skills_tool_dedup` in `sys.modules` (v0.23.3 has only
`dedup_skill_view` and `reset_skill_view_dedup`), so the import fails:

```
File ".../hermes-agent/agent/lazy_forward.py", line 11, in lazy_attr
    return getattr(importlib.import_module(module), name)
File ".../hermes-agent/agent/tool_executor.py", line 64, in <module>
    from tools.skills_tool_dedup import release_replaced_skill_view, release_replaced_skill_views
ImportError: cannot import name 'release_replaced_skill_view' from 'tools.skills_tool_dedup'
```

The worker's run is recorded `crashed` (`kanban dispatcher [default]: ... crashed=1`) and the task is
re-run by a fresh worker. The user-visible effect is a crashed task run and a repeated turn
(duplicated side effects of the tools that already ran in the crashed attempt).

## Where it comes from

- `release_replaced_skill_view` / `release_replaced_skill_views` were added by 34eb0dd5e7
  (`fix(skills): release a skill_view dedup entry the model only saw as a preview`, committed
  2026-11-20), which is not in v0.23.3.
- At v0.23.3, `agent/tool_executor.py` does not import `tools.skills_tool_dedup` at all, so an
  old process never had a reason to have the new names.
- The general class: any module the old process has not imported yet but whose new version imports a
  name added to a module the old process **has** imported. Lazy imports (`agent/lazy_forward.py`,
  function-local `from agent.tool_executor import ...` in `run_agent.py`,
  `agent/terminal_approval_batch.py`, `agent/inline_tool_executors.py`) make the window as long as the
  process lives.

## Reproduction

`tests/e2e/core/upgrade/handoff/test_handoff_from_n1.py::test_update_leaves_busy_gateway_pending_and_relaunches_after_the_work`
with `HERMES_E2E_UPGRADE_BASE=v0.23.3` against current `main` (seen on a branch whose diff is test/CI
only; the traceback is in the held worker's `errors.log`). The test fails because the held worker's run
ends `crashed` instead of completing on the old code.

## Possible directions (not evaluated)

- Make the moved-tree window safe for long-lived old processes: import `agent.tool_executor` (and the
  other lazily forwarded turn modules) eagerly at worker/agent start, so an old process never reads a
  new file.
- Or guard cross-module names added after a release with a fallback for one release cycle.
- Or have the update handoff stop/drain old workers before the checkout moves rather than after.

issues.title: [Bug]: gateway session-cache invalidation releases a mid-turn agent and aborts the in-flight stream (WinError 10058 / cache_evict_in_flight)
issues.body:
### Summary

When a gateway session-cache entry is invalidated while its turn is still streaming, `GatewaySessionAgentMixin._release_evicted_agent` soft-releases the evicted agent immediately. `release_clients()` retires the shared OpenAI client and closes per-request clients (`cache_evict_in_flight`), which force-closes the in-flight HTTP stream. The client observes `WinError 10058` / `ReadError`, the stream is retried, and the user sees a dropped/disconnected response.

### Where

- `gateway/session_execution.py` — `GatewaySessionAgentMixin._release_evicted_agent` (called from `_acquire` → `_release_evicted_agent(found.evicted)`, around line 226).
- `gateway/run_agent_cache.py` — `_evict_cached_agent` already has the correct guard:
  > "Never tear down an agent that's mid-turn — its client, sandbox and child subagents are in use."
  It checks `_running_agent_ids()` and defers via `state.turn.retired_agents`.
- The `session_execution` invalidation path does not perform that check.

### Trigger

`_lookup_cached_agent` invalidates the cached entry when `message_count changed` (cross-process write / session restore). `_pop_cached_agent_for_eviction()` pops it, then `_release_evicted_agent()` is called. If that agent's turn is still running, `release_clients()` retires/aborts its clients and the stream dies.

### Evidence (sanitized)

```
Shared OpenAI client retired (cache_evict, tcp_shutdown=0, fd_release=deferred_to_gc)
OpenAI client aborted (cache_evict_in_flight, shared=False, tcp_force_closed=1, deferred_close=stranger_thread)
Stream drop on attempt 1/3 — retrying ... error=[WinError 10058] ...
  http_status=200 bytes=958 chunks=19 elapsed=20.40s ttfb=19.68s finish_reason_seen=False
```

The release thread is named `agent-xproc-evict-...`, which comes from `session_execution.py`.

Server-side counters for that engine at the same time:

```
client_disconnect_total          5
request_success_total{abort}     5
request_success_total{error}     0
stream_overflow_total            0
```

The engine was healthy and streaming; the gateway side closed the socket.

### Suggested fix

Mirror the `_evict_cached_agent` guard in `_release_evicted_agent`:

```python
if id(agent) in self._runner._running_agent_ids():
    for key, running in self._runner._running_agent_items():
        if running is agent:
            state = self._runner._peek_session_state(key)
            if state is not None:
                if not any(retired is agent for retired in state.turn.retired_agents):
                    state.turn.retired_agents.append(agent)
                return
# ... existing _spawn_release_thread(...)
```

`_release_running_agent_state` drains `retired_agents` at the turn boundary, so the client is released after the stream completes instead of mid-stream.

### Regression test

Added `tests/gateway/test_session_execution_eviction_midturn.py`:

- runner with `SessionState.turn.agent = agent`
- `_release_evicted_agent(agent)` must **not** call `_release_evicted_agent_soft`
- the agent is appended to `state.turn.retired_agents`
- `_release_running_agent_state()` releases it at turn end
- an idle agent is still released immediately

Observed before the fix: the mid-turn test fails because the agent is released immediately. After the fix: both tests pass, and the related gateway cache/session tests pass (85 passed, 2 skipped).

### Environment

Windows 11, Hermes gateway + desktop, Python 3.14.9, local OpenAI-compatible engine.

issues.title: Printing check: a printer's bed is its bounding box, so round beds and excluded zones are taken as the full rectangle
issues.body:
## What's wrong

`--printer` takes a printer's build volume as the bounding box of `printable_area` by `printable_height` (`printer_settings` in `packages/cad/src/cad/_internal/dfm/printing.py`), and the fit is checked against a box (`lie` and `build_fit` in `_internal/meshops_printing.py`; the orientation ranking in `build123d/_dfm_printing.py`). So:
- **Round (delta) beds:** a part as big as the bed's square passes the build-volume check but can't be printed.
- **`bed_exclude_area`:** zones such as Bambu's 18 × 28 mm front-left corner on the X1C are ignored.

The code says it uses the bounding box. But `skills/cad/references/manufacturing-printing.md` says a part over the printer's volume is an error, which promises more than the check does on these printers.

## Options

| | What it covers | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Say so** | Nothing new. The report and the skill reference say "the bed's bounding box" when the volume comes from `--printer`. | ~15 min |
| **B. The real bed outline** | Round beds and any bed whose outline has no inward corners. Keep the `printable_area` polygon (not only its box) and test the part's footprint against it at each turn. A round bed only needs the smallest circle enclosing the footprint to fit the bed's circle. `fill_ratio` becomes the largest scale of the part that still fits. Both fit paths need it. | ~half a day + tests; ~0.2 s per check |
| **C. Excluded zones too** | `bed_exclude_area`: the footprint must also stay clear of each zone, so the usable bed is no longer one simple shape. | another ~half a day |

**Recommendation:** do A now. Do B if delta-printer users appear. Skip C: it only matters for a part within a zone's width of filling a Bambu bed, and testing the footprint's outer outline would wrongly refuse a part that wraps around a zone.

## Context

Found in review of #849, which shipped in 0.11.13 (#867). `bed_exclude_area` was named as a possible follow-up in #842.

issues.title: Sonos Beam Ultra: Speech Enhancement switch misreports and can't be turned off; no dialog level select (Arc Ultra fix only applies to Arc Ultra)
issues.body:
### The problem

On a **Sonos Beam Ultra**, the `switch.<name>_speech_enhancement` entity always shows **on** and cannot be turned off from Home Assistant, even when Speech Enhancement is **off** in the Sonos app. There is also no `select` entity for the speech enhancement level (Off / Low / Medium / High / Max), which the Sonos app offers on this model.

This is the same behaviour that was fixed for the Arc Ultra in #150116 (issue #142881). The Beam Ultra uses the same scheme as the Arc Ultra: a separate `SpeechEnhanceEnabled` boolean plus a 0–4 `DialogLevel`. But the integration only applies the fix to the exact model name `SONOS ARC ULTRA`, so the Beam Ultra falls back to the legacy boolean `dialog_level` path.

Verified directly with SoCo 0.32.1 on the device, with Speech Enhancement OFF in the Sonos app:

```
model_name: Sonos Beam Ultra
is_ultra_soundbar: True
dialog_level: True          <- what HA's switch reads (legacy path)
speech_enhance_enabled: False  <- the correct value
```

SoCo already supports the Beam Ultra here: SoCo/SoCo#1015 added it to `ULTRA_SOUNDBARS`, and it is included in soco 0.32.1, which HA 2026.11 ships.

### Where it comes from

`homeassistant/components/sonos/switch.py`:

```python
MODEL_FEATURE_SUBSTITUTIONS: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {
    MODEL_SONOS_ARC_ULTRA: {
        ATTR_SPEECH_ENHANCEMENT: ATTR_SPEECH_ENHANCEMENT_ENABLED,
    },
}
```

`homeassistant/components/sonos/select.py`: the `speech_dialog_level` select is created only when `speaker.model_name.upper() == MODEL_SONOS_ARC_ULTRA`.

### Suggested fix

Add `MODEL_SONOS_BEAM_ULTRA = "SONOS BEAM ULTRA"`, then apply it in both places:
- in `switch.py`, add it to `MODEL_FEATURE_SUBSTITUTIONS`
- in `select.py`, allow it for the `speech_dialog_level` select

Even better, base the decision on `soco.is_ultra_soundbar` rather than a model-name match, so future Ultra models work without changes.

I applied exactly this change locally as a custom component, and the switch and the level select then work correctly on the Beam Ultra. Details are below.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.11.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Sonos

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sonos/

issues.body:
Seen on self-hosted Hindsight 1.2.1 (rolled back to 1.1.0 since), checked again against v1.2.3 and `main` (80bd005fc). Paths are under `hindsight-api-slim/hindsight_api/`.

Setup: OpenAI-compatible provider serving a small Japanese model (sarashina3-mini), `HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_STRICT_SCHEMA_CONSOLIDATION=true`.

## What happens

Since #6164 (1.2.0, one answer per fact), consolidation batches sometimes never finish: the model emits whitespace until the 8000-token cap (~105 s) and the call fails with `OutputTooLongError`. 1.1.0 with the same model and settings does not do this.

## Why (from the source)

- `engine/structured_output.py`, `OpenAIStrictSchemaGenerator` (line ~77) sets `json_schema["required"] = list(properties)` — every field becomes required under strict mode, including `observation_text`.
- `engine/consolidation/prompts.py` (line ~121) tells the model: "`observation_text`: for repeats, changes or ends, the observation's text copied exactly. Leave it out for unrelated."

For an unrelated observation the grammar will not let the model close the object without `observation_text`, while the prompt tells it not to write one. A strong model writes `""` and moves on; a small model stalls and pads with whitespace until the cap.

When it does finish, we also saw field names (`observation_text`, `same_as_fact`, `kind`, `deletes`, …) stored as observation text (22 rows in one hour), which we did not see in the week before upgrading. That part we cannot tie to the source with certainty.

## Possible fixes

- Make the prompt match the schema: "for unrelated, set `observation_text` to an empty string", or
- make `observation_text` nullable / optional in the strict schema for the unrelated case.

Possibly related: #6673 (strict-schema replies that never end), #6019.

issues.title: [Bug] Subtitle import silently truncates overlong end-timestamp milliseconds
issues.body:
## Reproduction

On main at 8f6c113, import this subtitle through the dubbing subtitle importer:

```srt
1
00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,1234
Hello.
```

The shared `services.srt_parser.parse_srt` returns a cue ending at 2.123 seconds and reports zero skipped cues. The fourth digit is silently discarded. With an overlong start field instead, the timing line is not recognized and the malformed cue is not counted.

## Expected

Skip and count timestamps with more than three millisecond digits, preserving subsequent valid cues. Existing one- and two-digit millisecond support should remain intact.

## Cause and validation

`_TS` captures only 1–3 digits while the timing-line suffix accepts the remaining digits as trailing style hints. Eight regression cases reproduce incorrect skipping/counting for both endpoints and both accepted separators. The end-timestamp case changes the timing instead of exposing the malformed input.

Could you assign this issue to @isnaenihidayat? I have reproduced it and am preparing the regression test and fix.

issues.title: fit.py --fit crop: crop_content_off_centre fires on evenly spread, centred motion and suggests the anchor already in use
issues.body:
Found while reviewing main at 828efbb (crop_check came in with #585).

## What happens

`fit.py --fit crop` on a frame whose motion is spread evenly and centred reports `crop_content_off_centre`, and the remedy it names is the value already in use.

```
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=1280x720:r=30:d=12 -f lavfi -i sine=f=440:d=12 \
  -c:v libx264 -g 60 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -shortest src.mp4
python3 scripts/fit.py src.mp4 --aspect 9:16 --fit crop -o out.mp4 --json
```

Result (FFmpeg 6.1.1):

```
"crop_check": {"axis": "x", "discarded_fraction": 0.6833, "motion_outside": 0.5547,
               "detail_outside": 0.587, "centroid": 0.5026, "suggested_anchor": 0.5,
               "samples": 9, "verdict": "review"}
warning crop_content_off_centre: "55% of the sampled luma motion lies in the 68% of the frame
(x axis) the crop cuts away. ... --crop-x 0.5 centres the kept window on it"
```

The centroid is 0.50, the run used the default `--crop-x 0.5`, and the suggested anchor is 0.5.

## Why

In `crop_loss()` the motion branch is `motion_outside >= CROP_MOTION_OUTSIDE_WARN` (0.5) with no allowance for how much of the frame is cut. A 16:9 to 9:16 crop discards 68% of the width, so motion spread over the whole frame (a pan, handheld footage, a busy scene) always has more than half of it outside. The detail branch already compares against the discarded share (`detail_outside - discarded_fraction >= CROP_DETAIL_EXCESS_WARN`); the motion branch does not.

## Class

An advisory fires on input that gives it nothing to act on, and suggests the setting already in use. Callers that route on the warning code will re-run or ask the user for no reason, and the warning stops meaning anything on ordinary handheld footage.

## Suggested direction

- Motion branch: require an excess over the discarded share, as the detail branch does (the existing test's box at the left edge still gives about 1.0 against 0.68), and/or
- do not name `--crop-x V` / `--crop-y V` as the remedy when V equals the anchor the run used; say that only pad or blur keeps it.
- A regression test with evenly spread, centred motion (testsrc2) expecting verdict `ok`.

#613 rewrites the same function (per-sample review points). The same rule would apply to each sample there, so this is best fixed in or right after #613 rather than in a third branch.

issues.title: After 4.0: ways to make the 42 tools efficient to use
issues.body:
Ideas for after 4.0 (#632), recorded so they are not lost. None of this starts before the 4.0 numbers have come down. Each idea names what it would save a caller.

## 1. One front door: goal, project, preview, approval, run, check

Today an agent picks among 42 tools and about 1,100 flags, and the routing evals show that choosing the tool is where runs go wrong more often than the tool itself. A single entry point takes a goal in a few fields (source, platform, what to keep, captions or not), writes a `render.py` project, shows the plan and a low-resolution preview, waits for a yes, runs, and ends with `check.py`. The 42 tools become what the project is made of, not what the caller has to choose between.

Saves: tool choice, flag choice, the forgotten final check.

## 2. One encode for a chain of steps

After the rebuild each tool declares what it reads, writes and applies, so a chain (cut, reframe, captions, loudness, delivery preset) can be checked end to end before anything runs and, where the steps allow it, folded into one ffmpeg command. Today a chain is several encodes: slower, and each generation costs quality. Related: #357.

Saves: time (roughly one encode per step removed) and generation loss.

## 3. Fewer verbs on the surface

Present about eight verbs to a caller (trim, frame, sound, text, look, check, deliver, assemble) and keep the 42 tools as their modes. MCP already advertises a core set of 12; this goes one step further and makes the grouping the documented way in. `SKILL.md` gets shorter, which is also a standing constraint (its size budget).

Saves: routing mistakes, context spent on tool lists.

## 4. Deliver as one step

`deliver --platform X` = export preset, loudness to spec, content checks (black, frozen, silence, dropouts), size limit, and a contact sheet, with one result document. Related: #575, #579.

Saves: the three or four follow-up calls every delivery needs today.

## 5. Edit on a proxy, conform at the end

Long or 4K sources: do every decision (cuts, crops, caption placement) on a small proxy with fast encodes, record the decisions in the project, and apply them once to the original. `proxy.py` and plans exist; the missing part is carrying the decisions across.

Saves: most of the waiting on long sources.

## 6. The project file as the memory of an edit

Every step appends to one project file: what was asked, what ran, what was measured. Re-running, undoing one step, or handing the edit to a person or another agent starts from that file instead of from a chat history.

Saves: redoing work after a context loss; makes review possible (#581).

## 7. Show, do not describe

After each step that changes the picture, attach a frame or a contact sheet and the before/after numbers automatically, so the caller checks the result instead of trusting `verified`. Related: #581, #570.

Saves: the errors nobody sees until the upload.

## 8. Learn which tools are used

An opt-in local log of which tools and flags a machine actually runs (no network). The first use is deciding what to prune or stop guaranteeing.

Saves: maintaining what nobody uses.

## Order suggested

1 and 4 first (largest effect for a caller, built from parts that exist), then 2 (needs the rebuilt engine), then 3 and 6. 5, 7 and 8 as they fit.

issues.title: citation_compliance_agent: some checks still assume APA 7th for every citation style
issues.body:
## Problem

`academic-paper/agents/citation_compliance_agent.md` checks citations in five styles (APA 7th, Chicago 17th, MLA 9th, IEEE, Vancouver), but several of its checks still apply APA 7th rules to every style. The review of #1087 found these; #1087 guards only Common Auto-Corrections, the rows of Common Citation Error Patterns, and two lines of the Step 4 DOI/URL Check.

Known places on `main` after #1087:

- `### 3. DOI/URL Verification` asks for "DOI included if available" and "No trailing period after DOI/URL" for every reference. MLA 9th lists a DOI as optional, and MLA and Chicago entries can end with a period.
- Step 4 of the Detailed Execution Algorithm still checks every DOI against `https://doi.org/xxxxx`, and `Core Verification Rules by Format` gives Chicago 17th as "URL or DOI" without saying when a missing DOI is an error.

A literal reading can flag or change a correct MLA or Chicago reference.

## Done when

The file has one rule that decides each format check by the selected style, every check in the file follows it, and a pass over the whole file lists any check that still assumes APA 7th.

issues.body:
## Problem

When `neko-plugin check` finds a missing repository support file (`README.md`, `tests/test_smoke.py`, `.vscode/*`, `.github/workflows/*`, `.gitignore`), it suggests:

```text
fix: neko-plugin setup-repo <plugin_id> --github-actions
```

`setup-repo` resolves a bare plugin id only under the plugins root (`plugin/plugins` by default). For a plugin that lives anywhere else, which is the usual layout for a plugin with its own Git repository, the suggested command fails:

```text
[FAIL] plugin.toml not found for plugin '<plugin_id>': <checkout>/plugin/plugins/<plugin_id>/plugin.toml
```

## Where

[`release_cmd._suggest_fix`](https://github.com/Project-N-E-K-O/N.E.K.O/blob/69d8b5e52bd49b3e7db8f87c0a3be07c4031d3e3/plugin/neko_plugin_cli/commands/release_cmd.py#L606) returns `f"neko-plugin setup-repo {label} --github-actions"`, where `label` is the plugin id.

## Suggested fix

When `plugin_dir` is known, suggest the plugin path instead of the id, quoted so that paths with spaces work in bash, PowerShell and cmd:

```python
target = f'"{plugin_dir}"' if plugin_dir is not None else label
return f"neko-plugin setup-repo {target} --github-actions"
```

#3808 uses the same form for its new stale agent-kit hint. Extend a `check` test with a plugin outside the plugins root and assert that the suggested command succeeds.

Impact: only the suggested command text; `check` results and exit codes are unaffected.

Context: found while working on #3808, which leaves this for a separate change.

— DevNeko (assisted by Claude Opus 5.5)

issues.title: neko-plugin skill text guards: code-fence tracking ignores nested fences
issues.body:
## Context

`plugin/tests/unit/test_neko_plugin_agent_guides.py` (added in #3806) guards the neko-plugin skill text with simple regexes. Its `_FENCE` pattern toggles "inside a code fence" on any line starting with ``` or ~~~, regardless of the opening fence's character or length.

## Limitation

If a skill document nests fences (a four-backtick or `~~~` block wrapping a three-backtick example), the inner fence line closes the outer block early. Two checks share `_FENCE` and are affected:

- the `[checkout only]` section detection (a `#` comment inside the outer block could be read as a heading);
- the scan for bare `neko-plugin <subcommand>` lines inside code fences, so an unregistered subcommand after the inner fence would not be reported.

No skill file or agent-guide template uses nested fences today, so nothing is missed now. This was raised in review of #3806 and deliberately left out to keep the guard simple.

## Suggested fix (when a nested example is first added)

Track the opening fence's character and length, and close only on a line with the same character, at least that length, and nothing but whitespace after it (CommonMark rule). Add a nested-fence regression case for both checks.

— DevNeko (assisted by Claude Opus 5.5)

issues.title: Telegram bot webhook mode cannot start: run_webhook is awaited but synchronous; webhook_port ignored
issues.body:
## What happens

Telegram bots in webhook mode (`webhook_url` set) cannot start.

`TelegramBot.start()` in `src/praisonai-bot/praisonai_bot/bots/telegram.py` (~L1508) does:

```python
await self._application.run_webhook(listen="0.0.0.0", port=8443, ...)
```

In python-telegram-bot 20+ (`>=20.0` is the declared floor; 22.5 checked), `Application.run_webhook` is a **synchronous** call that starts and owns its own event loop. Calling it from inside the bot's running loop fails, and its `None` return cannot be awaited.

## Second defect

The port is hardcoded to `8443`, so `BotConfig.webhook_port` (default `8080`) and the YAML `webhook_port` field are ignored.

## Fix

Inside the existing loop, use the async pieces instead: `await app.initialize()`, `await app.updater.start_webhook(listen=..., port=config.webhook_port or 8443, url_path=..., webhook_url=...)`, `await app.start()`, and the matching stop calls in `stop()`. Add a test that starts webhook mode against a mocked `Updater` and checks the configured port is used.

issues.title: Qwen3.8 campaign: separate recipe from load path for the loadpath-333 concept arm
issues.body:
The `loadpath-333` stage of `scripts/qwen38_a100_campaign.py` qualified the Qwen3.8-27B composite (ImageTextToText) load path on one 80 GB A100 at main `b9252dc`. The runner's overall verdict was **FAIL**, and the only cause was the concept arm's quality gates.

## What passed
- Pristine text-backbone logit parity between CausalLM and ImageTextToText was exact (max abs error 0.0, top-token agreement 1.0).
- Memory admission with the vision weights passed (+0.92 GB).
- The refusal edit on the composite path passed every gate.
- Edited checkpoints of both arms reload under both auto classes.
- GSQ resolves the text backbone (496/496).

## What failed
The concept arm `user/campaign-pain-pilot` (diff_means) used `layer_select: preset all`, so it excised the direction at all 64 layers, including 0–3 and the last layers. Its controls were underpowered (n=20) and validation returned `fail`. The edited model degenerated:
- perplexity 3.15 → about 3.0e5;
- coherence 0 and capability 0/6;
- invalid outputs 0% → 83%;
- refusal 94.5% → 0%.

This looks like a recipe effect, since all-layer removal of a weak pilot direction is expected to be destructive. But the run had no causal-path control for this arm, so path-independence is not demonstrated.

## Proposal
Add a way to separate the two. Either:
- rerun the concept arm with data-driven layer selection (`cv_auc`); or
- run the concept arm once on the CausalLM path with the same recipe.

Record which variant ran in the stage evidence. Quality gates should keep reporting without vetoing the operator's edit.

issues.title: Phase memory admission cannot model the qwen3_5_text recurrent scan workspace
issues.body:
On Qwen3.8-27B (`qwen3_5_text`, hybrid linear-attention), every concept and edit phase logs this warning and then proceeds in default mode:

```
PHASE MEMORY ADMISSION WARNING: phase '<baseline|probe|validate|excise|verify>' on cuda:0; estimated shortfall 0 bytes (0.00 GiB) plus unknown demand; ... unmodelled demand: Cannot model phase demand: ValueError: unmodelled qwen3_5_text recurrent scan backend: only the installed Transformers torch fallback workspace is bounded; set OBLITERATUS_PHASE_ADMISSION=off to explicitly bypass admission.
```

## Evidence
From one bf16 run on a single 80 GB A100 (main `b9252dc`, torch 2.13.0+cu130, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2, causal-conv1d 1.7.0):
- load peak: 54.07 GB (CausalLM) and 54.75 GB (ImageTextToText);
- stage receipt peak during edits, reloads and evaluation: **55,974 MiB**.

Nothing ran out of memory. But in default mode the admission check cannot bound these phases, and `strict` mode would refuse them.

## Proposal
Model the recurrent-scan workspace for the installed FLA/causal-conv1d backends, as is already done for the torch fallback, so phase admission can give a real estimate for Qwen3.5/3.8 hybrid models. Add a CPU test with a tiny `qwen3_5_text` config.

issues.title: [PERF] #4989 (fix of #4955) incomplete: EXL3 BF16 native path is launch-bound - ~12 eager ops per linear for the per-row pre-scale make bf16 decode 2x slower than fp16 (8.7 vs 4.4 ms/step, 96 vs 33 us per linear on sm_120)
issues.body:
Found on `main` @ 7b8f12785, RTX 5090 (sm_120), torch 2.15 + CUDA 13.2. GPU otherwise idle.

### What is wrong
#4989 (fix of #4955) removed the host sync from the EXL3 BF16 path. Decode in BF16 (the default load dtype for Llama-3/Qwen EXL3 checkpoints) is still **2x slower than the same checkpoint in fp16**, and 2.4x slower than the dense bf16 model. The cause is now CPU launch overhead. `ExllamaV3Linear._native_bf16_input` + `_rescale_native_output` (`gptqmodel/nn_modules/exllamav3.py:411-449`) run about 10 eager tensor ops per linear per forward:
`vector_norm(inf)`, `.float()`, `div`, `frexp`, `ones_like` x2, `ldexp`, `where`, `x / scale`, `.to(fp16)`, then `result.to(fp32)`, `* scale`, `.to(bf16)`.

At decode (M=1) each of these is a microsecond-scale kernel, but each costs a full dispatch + launch on the host. `torch.profiler` over 20 calls of one `gate_proj` (4096 -> 14336): GPU time is 46 us/call (EXL3 GEMM 30 us + elementwise ~16 us), while host time is **209 us/call**. The per-call wall clock is GPU-starved.

### Numbers
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct truncated to 8 decoder layers, `EXL3Config(bits=4)` quantized with GPTQModel, AUTO -> `ExllamaV3Linear`. Batch 1, manual `DynamicCache` decode loop, CUDA-event medians:

| | decode step bs1 | decode step bs8 | prefill 2048 | `generate()` 128 tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dense HF bf16 | 3.60 ms | 4.10 ms | 39.3 ms | 242 tok/s |
| EXL3 fp16 | 4.38 ms | 4.40 ms | 35.7 ms | 209 tok/s |
| **EXL3 bf16** | **8.67 ms** | 8.55 ms | 46.4 ms | **111 tok/s** |

Single `mlp.gate_proj`, M=1, wall clock per call (200 calls, synchronized at the end): bf16 **96.2 us**, fp16 33.0 us. Wrapping the two helpers in `torch.compile` only reaches 86 us (still dispatch-bound) and is bit-identical to the current output. CUDA-event per-module times: q/o/gate/down at M=1 are 112/106/115/119 us in bf16 vs 42/42/57/59 us in fp16 (dense bf16: 23/23/80/83 us).

### Repro
```python
m = GPTQModel.load("<EXL3 4-bit Llama-3.1-8B ckpt>", backend=BACKEND.AUTO, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
lin = m.model.model.layers[0].mlp.gate_proj            # ExllamaV3Linear
x = torch.randn(1, 1, 4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
import time
with torch.inference_mode():
    for xx in (x, x.half()):
        for _ in range(10): lin(xx)
        torch.cuda.synchronize(); t = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(200): lin(xx)
        torch.cuda.synchronize(); print(xx.dtype, (time.perf_counter() - t) / 200 * 1e6, "us")
# torch.bfloat16 96.2 us / torch.float16 33.0 us
```

### Suggested fix
Do the pre-scale in one launch: a small fused CUDA/Triton op computing the row amax, the power-of-two scale and the fp16 cast, writing `x_fp16` and `scale`. Do the rescale in one more fused op, or fold it into the EXL3 GEMM epilogue (it is a per-row multiply). That brings bf16 down to two extra launches per linear instead of about 12. The math stays bit-identical: power-of-two scaling, then one rounding.

### Test that should have caught it
#4989's test asserts there is no host sync. Nothing compares bf16 vs fp16 EXL3 decode latency. An M=1 bound such as "bf16 <= 1.3x fp16 per linear" would catch the launch overhead.

### Severity
Medium [PERF]: the default dtype of EXL3 Llama/Qwen checkpoints decodes at half the speed of fp16.

issues.title: [DocDB] yb-master never starts again after the fd limit is restored, once a start hit Too many open files in sys catalog bootstrap: WAL files missing
issues.body:
Jira Link: [DB-26572](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-26572)
## Description

A yb-master that runs out of file descriptors once during sys catalog bootstrap can be left unable to start again, even after the fd limit is back to normal. Running out of fds is only the trigger, and that start failing is expected. The bug is what follows. Every later start, with the normal fd limit restored, fails WAL replay with `WAL files missing`, so the master needs manual recovery. There is no power loss and no crash, only one start that hit EMFILE.

Seen on 2024.2.12.0-b52 (aarch64, Linux), with `durable_wal_write` on.

### Observed

The start that runs out of fds dies with:

```
F master_main.cc:144] IO error (yb/util/env_posix.cc:1125): Unable to initialize catalog manager: Failed to initialize sys tables async: <fs_data_dir>/yb-data/master/wals/table-sys.catalog.uuid/tablet-00000000000000000000000000000000: Too many open files (system error 24)
```

Earlier in that same start the log shows, in this order:

```
Bootstrap replayed 1/1 log segments. Read operations: 573, ... Last read committed op id: 1.573, last entry metadata: { ... offset: 259550 ... }
ReplayState: Previous OpId: 1.573, Committed OpId: 1.573, ... Flushed Regular: 1.573, ...
.../wal-000000001: Truncating file from size: 258048 to size: 258048. Preallocated size: 0. Size on disk: 1048576
Successfully rebuilt footer for segment: .../wal-000000001 (valid entries through byte offset 259708)
```

Every start after that, with the normal fd limit, fails:

```
F master_main.cc:144] Illegal state (yb/tablet/tablet_bootstrap.cc:1703): Unable to initialize catalog manager: Failed to initialize sys tables async: Failed log replay. Reason: WAL files missing, or committed op id is incorrect. Expected both term and index of prev_op_id to be greater than or equal to the corresponding components of committed_op_id. prev_op_id=1.566, committed_op_id=1.573
```

The EMFILE start had replayed the WAL through op 1.573, so the WAL was complete before that start. After it, the segment ends at op 1.566.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start 3 yb-masters (RF=3) and 1 yb-tserver on one host with `--durable_wal_write=true --log_segment_size_mb=1`.
2. Keep sys catalog writes going with a CREATE TABLE / DROP TABLE loop in ysqlsh.
3. Run `yb-admin flush_sys_catalog`, then stop one follower master.
4. Start it again. When its open fd count reaches N during startup (N=37 in the run that reproduced), run `prlimit --pid <pid> --nofile=<N+8>:`.
5. After it dies with `Too many open files`, start it again with the normal fd limit.

The window is narrow. It reproduced in 1 of 11 such starts on RF=3. Most EMFILE starts die at other points and restart fine.

Controls on the same setup:
- kill -9 at the same startup points: 15 restarts, none failed to start.
- Restarts with no fault: 4, none failed to start.

In a longer run the same thing happened during a rolling upgrade. A master lost about 40 sys catalog ops (`prev_op_id=32.4264, committed_op_id=33.4304`) and never started again.

### Expected

A start that fails with EMFILE should not change the WAL so that later starts cannot replay it. The next start with a normal fd limit should come up.

### Related

#34197 has the same replay error, but after power loss.

## Issue Type

kind/bug

## Warning

- [x] I confirm this issue does not contain any sensitive information.

issues.title: CLI exposes raw traceback when a DeepSeek connection fails
issues.body:
## Summary

When the DeepSeek provider connection fails, the terminal CLI prints a full Python traceback and exits instead of showing a concise actionable error.

## Environment

- `waku-agent 0.1.12`
- Python 3.14 on Linux
- `WAKU_PROVIDER=deepseek`
- Waku Memory disabled

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a valid DeepSeek API key.
2. Start Waku with `WAKU_PROVIDER=deepseek waku`.
3. Send a prompt when the provider connection encounters a transport/TLS failure.

## Actual behavior

The retrieval gate reports a fail-open event such as:

```
gate · retrieve — gate failed open (APIConnectionError)
```

The main model request then raises `openai.APIConnectionError`, and the CLI prints the complete Python traceback, including HTTP client internals.

## Expected behavior

- Keep the retrieval gate's fail-open behavior if that is intentional.
- Catch the main provider connection error at the CLI boundary.
- Print a short actionable message, for example:

```
error: model connection failed; check network or proxy settings and retry
```

- Exit non-zero.
- Preserve technical details in the local trace or an explicit debug mode rather than printing them by default.

## Scope

The underlying TLS EOF may be environmental or upstream-related. This report is specifically about graceful CLI handling of an expected provider connection failure, not an attribution of the transport failure itself.

issues.title: [FEA]: Configurable extra HTTP headers for the openai-compatible provider
issues.body:
## Problem to solve

Some OpenAI-compatible gateways reject requests that lack a routing header. OpenCode Go is one: a request from SkillEvaluator's chat client (`rubric-eval`, Tier 1 LLM checks, the judge) returns

```
HTTP 400  MissingSessionID: Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently.
```

even for a minimal chat completion, so `SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` cannot be used with that gateway. SkillEvaluator already supports OpenCode as a Tier 3 agent (see #763), but the evaluator's own LLM client has no way to send custom headers; the only `extra_headers` use in `inference/client.py` is an Anthropic beta flag.

## Proposed approach

Add `SKILL_EVAL_LLM_EXTRA_HEADERS`: a JSON object of header names to string values, sent as `default_headers` by the `openai-compatible` chat client.

- A `{uuid}` placeholder in a value is replaced with one random UUID per client, so session-routed gateways get a stable id.
- Other providers (`openai`, `nv_build`, ...) ignore the variable, so headers are never sent to native endpoints.
- Invalid JSON or non-string values fail with a clear error.

Example:

```bash
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=openai-compatible
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_BASE_URL=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_API_KEY=...
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_EXTRA_HEADERS='{"x-opencode-session": "{uuid}"}'
```

Alternatives considered: a dedicated `x-opencode-session` option (too gateway-specific), or a Python-only hook (not usable from CI). A prototype is ready on a branch and I will open a PR referencing this issue.

## Additional context

Out of scope: the embedding client and the Tier 3 in-container agents, which build their own clients. With the prototype, `rubric-eval` against OpenCode Go with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` completed all nine criteria. No credentials or private data are included.

issues.title: [embedding] Point integrators and coding agents at the supported surface (AGENTS.md, llms.txt, non-contract notices)
issues.body:
When a developer asks an AI coding agent to "embed GAIA in my app", nothing at the repository root points it at the supported integration surface, so it reads the code and patches the most visible hooks — `Agent`, `_execute_tool`, `process_query`. Those are internals with no stability promise, and integrations built on them break on routine releases.

**Proposal:** make the supported path the first thing both people and coding agents see.

- **`AGENTS.md`:** add an "Integrating GAIA into another application" section that names, in order, the sidecar contract, `openapi.gaia.json`, the embed guide, and the `@amd-gaia/gaia` npm client.
- **`llms.txt`** (and optionally `llms-full.txt`) on the docs site, listing those same pages.
- **Non-contract notices:** mark `Agent._execute_tool`, `process_query` and similar internals as "not a stable surface for embedding applications" in their docstrings, and add a matching banner to extension docs that use them — with a pointer to the supported alternative where one exists or is planned (e.g. #4590 for tool policy).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A coding agent asked to embed GAIA in an app is directed to the sidecar contract by files at the repository root.
- [ ] Internals commonly patched by integrators carry a visible non-contract notice.
- [ ] `llms.txt` is served from the docs site and lists the integration pages.

Part of #4589. Depends on #5173 (the embed guide) for a page to point at.

<details>
<summary>🔍 Technical details</summary>

State at `5e23720`:
- No `llms.txt` at the repo root or under `docs/`.
- `AGENTS.md` has no section on embedding GAIA; it covers contributing only.
- `.claude/skills/integrate-hub-agent/SKILL.md` is already agent-agnostic, and `hub/agents/gaia/npm/SKILL.md` covers the flagship sidecar — but both are only discoverable from inside a Claude Code session in this repo, not by an agent working in the integrator's own project.
- `_execute_tool` (`src/gaia/agents/base/agent.py`) is a private method whose docstring describes internal contracts (the `NOT_EXECUTED` sentinel, stand-ins copying it by attribute assignment) with no warning against external use.
</details>

issues.title: Middleware edits are dropped when a tool returns a CallToolResult
issues.body:
### What happened?

An `on_call_tool` middleware that edits the result after `call_next` works for ordinary tools. For a tool that returns an `mcp_types.CallToolResult`, the middleware sees its edits, but the client still receives the tool's original content and structured content. So a redaction middleware like the one below leaks whatever those tools return. Returning `result.model_copy(update=...)` instead of editing in place loses the edits too. This also happens on the 4.2.0 release.

I expected both tools to print `redacted`. The script prints:

```
plain redacted {'token': 'redacted'}
protocol s3cr3t {'token': 's3cr3t'}
```

### Example Code

```Python
import asyncio

from mcp_types import CallToolResult, TextContent

from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP
from fastmcp.server.middleware import Middleware


class Redact(Middleware):
    async def on_call_tool(self, context, call_next):
        result = await call_next(context)
        result.content = [TextContent(type="text", text="redacted")]
        result.structured_content = {"token": "redacted"}
        return result


mcp = FastMCP(middleware=[Redact()])


@mcp.tool
def plain() -> dict:
    return {"token": "s3cr3t"}


@mcp.tool
def protocol() -> CallToolResult:
    return CallToolResult(
        content=[TextContent(type="text", text="s3cr3t")],
        structured_content={"token": "s3cr3t"},
    )


async def main():
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        for name in ("plain", "protocol"):
            result = await client.call_tool(name)
            print(name, result.content[0].text, result.structured_content)


asyncio.run(main())
```

### Version Information

```Text
FastMCP version:                                 4.2.1.dev5+8c0e10ff
MCP version:                                                   2.3.0
Python version:                                              3.12.16
Platform:                               macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit
```

issues.title: Delegate route guard rejects valid YAML 1.1 directive and indentless block sequences
issues.body:
OMH 4.0.6 and current main (6906258099fda4065c98fa13addca6663af06c13) reject valid Hermes configuration with config_unreadable before any delegate dispatch. Two independent minimal inputs:

```yaml
%YAML 1.1
---
delegation:
  model: example
```

```yaml
fallback_providers:
- model: example
  provider: custom
delegation:
  model: example
```

Installed Hermes 0.23.0 hermes_yaml.safe_load accepts both. scan_config in src/plugin_bundle/omh/route_endpoint_guard.py treats the directive and the indentless sequence entry as unexpected root keys. Removing only one form from a document containing both still refuses. Formatting both away in memory preserves parsed values and passes the guard.

Proposed fix: recognize a single leading YAML 1.1 directive followed by document start, and indentless sequences under untracked empty root keys. Continue refusing multiple documents, duplicate keys, sequence-valued model/delegation, unsupported directives and endpoint ambiguity. A local patch passes 11 new regression cases plus the existing routing/endpoint suites; carried as a hash-guarded Nix compatibility patch rather than rewriting user configuration.

issues.title: [BUG]: Script lint skips valid UTF-8-BOM Python scripts and reports them as passed
issues.body:
### What happened?

The advisory script linter silently skips a valid Python file when it begins with a UTF-8 byte-order mark. On SkillEvaluator `96f03c1abf0e801a1d062d67737f35465c6df219` (version 0.9.0), the same `import sys\nprint(sys.argv)\n` source produces `flat_script`, `missing_shebang`, and `no_input_validation` findings without the BOM. With `EF BB BF` prefixed, the CLI produces no findings and says `All 1 script(s) passed lint checks`. Both runs exit 0 because this lint is advisory.

### Reproduction steps

Create a temporary valid skill with `scripts/example.py` containing `import sys\nprint(sys.argv)\n`, then run:

```bash
skillevaluator lint-scripts /tmp/plain-skill -r json -o /tmp/plain-report
```

Write the same source bytes prefixed by `EF BB BF` into a second skill and run the command with a different output directory:

```bash
skillevaluator lint-scripts /tmp/bom-skill -r json -o /tmp/bom-report
```

Inspect `results[0].findings` and `results[0].success_details` in the JSON reports. The plain file has three advisory findings; the BOM file has none and is reported as passed. Both commands return 0. The behavior was reproduced through the public CLI on the commit above using a temporary synthetic fixture.

Expected: a single initial UTF-8 BOM does not prevent AST checks from running; the advisory severity and exit behavior stay unchanged.

### SkillEvaluator version or commit

`96f03c1abf0e801a1d062d67737f35465c6df219` (`0.9.0`)

### Environment

- macOS arm64
- Python 3.13.15
- uv development environment (`uv sync --frozen --python 3.13 --all-extras`)
- Synthetic local skill; no provider or credentials

### Before submitting

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct.
- [x] I searched open issues for a duplicate. Related historical BOM reports concern `SKILL.md` frontmatter, not Python script lint.

issues.title: [BUG]: Task-list helper loses task text and changes saved status when descriptions contain status words
issues.body:
### What happened?

The bundled task-list helper accepts a task description containing status-shaped parenthetical text, but `list` interprets a matching word inside the description as the serialized status. For example, adding `Investigate (completed) labels after merge` creates a pending task with the full description. The next `list` reports it as completed with description `Investigate`, then rewrites the Markdown state file with that corrupted task.

Expected: only the final serialized status suffix should determine status; the full description should remain unchanged after listing and reloading.

### Reproduction steps

On commit `abac7c5f575d646cd0d8fe1c5fb7edcc3a46af70`, use a fresh temporary state path:

```sh
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
export TASK_LIST_STATE_PATH="$tmpdir/todo.md"
uv run --no-sync python src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/task-list/scripts/tasks.py add --content 'Investigate (completed) labels after merge'
uv run --no-sync python src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/task-list/scripts/tasks.py list
cat "$TASK_LIST_STATE_PATH"
```

Observed: `list` prints `Completed` and truncates the description to `Investigate`; the saved file moves the task to the Completed section. The commands use only a synthetic local task and require no credentials or provider access.

### SkillEvaluator version or commit

`0.9.0`, commit `abac7c5f575d646cd0d8fe1c5fb7edcc3a46af70` (upstream `main` at reproduction).

### Environment

macOS 26, arm64, Python 3.13.15; source checkout, run with the repository's `uv` environment.

### Before submitting

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have searched the [open issues](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Abug) and found no duplicate of this report

issues.title: [BUG]: Packaged API caller builds invalid URLs for scalar path values containing spaces or reserved characters
issues.body:
### What happened?

The packaged API caller substitutes an OpenAPI path parameter with its raw string value. A plain `id=plain-id` works, but `id=red blue` produces `/items/red blue`; the CLI fails with `URL can't contain control characters` before the loopback endpoint receives the request. Reserved characters in scalar identifiers can also become URL syntax instead of remaining path data.

Expected: each scalar path value is encoded as one path segment while the authored path separators and query parameters remain unchanged.

### Reproduction steps

Using a synthetic OpenAPI fixture served only on loopback, define `GET /items/{id}` with operation ID `getItem` and a server URL of `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Then run from the repository root:

```sh
uv run --no-sync python src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/api-caller/scripts/call_api.py \
  --spec http://127.0.0.1:<port>/openapi.json --operation getItem --params '{"id":"plain-id"}'
uv run --no-sync python src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/api-caller/scripts/call_api.py \
  --spec http://127.0.0.1:<port>/openapi.json --operation getItem --params '{"id":"red blue"}'
```

Observed on the current checkout: the plain control exits 0 and the loopback server receives `/items/plain-id`; the space value exits 1 with an invalid-URL control-character error and never reaches the endpoint. The fixture and requests are local and require no credentials or external API access.

### SkillEvaluator version or commit

`0.9.0`, commit `64808e9b01073643e76da212ff3a7781a1a514ec` (upstream `main` at reproduction).

### Environment

macOS 27.0.1, arm64, Python 3.13.15; source checkout, run with the repository's `uv` environment.

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

issues.title: tracekit audit: read Qwen Code's saved sessions
issues.body:
`tracekit audit` replays a coding agent's past tool calls through the policy and counts what it would have held or denied. It reads Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline and Gemini CLI (`READERS`, `tracekit/audit.py` L450-457). For any other agent it says `no reader for qwen's sessions yet; turn them into a calls file and use --calls FILE --agent qwen` (`_no_reader`, L477-479).

Qwen Code is a fork of Gemini CLI (`tracekit/agent_hooks.py` L45). Tracekit already hooks it (`tracekit init --dev --v2 --agent qwen`, [coding agents](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/blob/main/docs/coding-agents.md)) and maps its tool names (`QWEN_TOOLS`, `agent_hooks.py` L164). A reader would let a Qwen Code user see what the policy would have done with their past sessions, as Gemini CLI users can.

Not checked yet: where Qwen Code keeps its sessions and in what format. It may write Gemini CLI's `chats` files, which `_gemini` (`audit.py` L266) reads, or its own.

**What to do**

1. Record a short real Qwen Code session with a few tool calls (a shell command, a file read, an edit). Say which Qwen Code version and OS you used, where the files were, and what a record looks like. Commit a trimmed copy, with nothing private in it, as test data.
2. Add a `"qwen"` entry to `READERS`: its default folder (honour the environment variable Qwen Code uses for its home, if it has one, as the Gemini entry does with `$GEMINI_CLI_HOME`), a description, and a reader. If the format is Gemini CLI's, reuse `_gemini`. If not, write a reader like the others: `(time, session, tool, args)` for each call, `None` for a malformed record, a copy of a call counted once.
3. Tool names: audit maps each call's name as that agent's hook does (`hook_tool`, `audit.py` L568), so Qwen Code's `run_shell_command` is decided as `Bash`. Check that in a test.
4. Docs: `docs/audit.md` names the agents with readers in the ROOT and `--agent` bullets (L34-37, L42-51) and the folders table (L77-83); add a "Qwen Code's reader" paragraph like Gemini CLI's (L126); and add Qwen Code to the readers the `docs/limits.md` row at L941 lists. The help text is built from `READERS`, so it follows.

**Acceptance**

- `tracekit audit ROOT --agent qwen`, and `tracekit audit` with no ROOT when Qwen Code's folder exists, count the calls of the recorded session; the tests are built from that recording.
- A shell call the default policy denies is reported as denied.
- If the format repeats a call (a resumed or rewritten session), it counts once.
- `make lint` and `tests/test_audit.py` pass.

Commits need a DCO sign-off (`git commit -s`). Comment here with your Qwen Code version before you start.

issues.title: Claude Agent SDK: check whether PreToolUse fires for Write and Edit in acceptEdits and default modes
issues.body:
anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript#493 (still open) reports that the TypeScript Agent SDK auto-approves Write and Edit inside the working directory without consulting `canUseTool` or `permissions.deny`, in both `acceptEdits` and `default` modes. For PreToolUse hooks its table says: in `acceptEdits` the hook never fires for Write; in `default` it fires, but only after the write is done.

Tracekit's Claude Agent SDK integration gates every call through the PreToolUse hook (`tracekit_hooks`, `tracekit/integrations/claude_agent_sdk.py` L110). Its docstring (L13-14) says the CLI skips `can_use_tool` for calls its permission mode or allow rules approve, "while PreToolUse runs for every call". If the report also holds for the Python SDK and the Claude Code CLI it drives, Write and Edit in the working directory skip the gate. In `acceptEdits` they would be neither decided nor recorded: the PostToolUse handler (`post`, L157-159) records only calls `pre` let through. In `default`, a deny would come after the file was written.

Not verified yet: the report is against the TypeScript SDK, and Tracekit's integration is the Python one (tested range `claude-agent-sdk>=0.2.165,<0.3`, `tracekit/autowire.py` L368).

**To check, with a real run** (it needs a Claude login or API key):

1. A Python Agent SDK session with `tracekit_hooks(...)`, in `permission_mode="acceptEdits"` and then `"default"`.
2. Ask it to Write a new file in the working directory, and to Edit one.
3. Is a `policy.decision` recorded before each write? Does a policy that denies Write to that path block it?
4. Repeat with Claude Code itself (the CLI, with `tracekit init --dev --v2` hooks), as a control.

Say which SDK and CLI versions you ran.

**If it reproduces:**

- a row in `docs/limits.md` saying what isn't gated and what to do (for example `permission_mode="default"` with an explicit `ask` rule, if that works);
- a test with the real SDK, if CI can run one;
- a comment on the upstream issue with the Python result.

**If it doesn't,** say so here with the versions, and on the upstream issue too: that's useful to them.

Earlier: #529.
